evidence.title: Exploring Patient Perspectives, Engagement, and Output Quality in Doctor-Supervised Use of Artificial Intelligence During Informed Consent Consultation With ChatGPT and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG): Quantitative Exploratory Study
evidence.outcome: Hallucination rate and physician-rated response quality, RAG vs native ChatGPT
evidence.effect: Hallucinations 5/52 (10%) with RAG vs 15/39 (38%) native, P=.002; RAG better on relevance, accuracy, clarity, completeness, evidence-based, length (all P<.001).
evidence.quote: We observed significantly fewer hallucinations in the RAG group versus in the native ChatGPT group (5 out of 52 [10%] vs 15 out of 39, 38%; Table 8 ).

evidence.title: Transforming oncology clinical trial matching through neuro-symbolic, multi-agent AI and an oncology-specific knowledge graph: a prospective evaluation in 3804 patients
evidence.venue: ESMO real world data and digital oncology

evidence.title: Community Learning Ledgers for Cancer Navigation in Small Island Developing States
evidence.outcome: Actionable navigation citing verified Caribbean facilities, same model with vs without governance
evidence.effect: Same foundation model scored 100% with governance and 54% without (P≤.001); CaribChat cited verified Caribbean facilities in 28/28 vs 10/28 ChatGPT, 9/28 OpenEvidence
evidence.quote: The same model scored 100% with governance and 54% without (P≤.001).
evidence.sample_unit: patient screening queries (plus 207 community sessions descriptively classified)
evidence.country: Caribbean (ten jurisdictions, led by Trinidad and Tobago)

evidence.title: Evaluating a Nationally Localized AI Chatbot for Personalized Primary Care Guidance: Insights from the HomeDOCtor Deployment in Slovenia
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of RAG-grounded HomeDOCtor versus stand-alone ChatGPT-4o on Slovenian national exam questions
evidence.effect: HomeDOCtor with RAG over curated guidelines achieved 90.7% versus 80.7% for stand-alone ChatGPT-4o (p = 0.0135).
evidence.quote: On international benchmarks, the system achieved ≥95% Top-1 diagnostic accuracy, comparable to leading medical AI platforms, and significantly outperformed stand-alone ChatGPT-4o in the national context (90.7% vs. 80.7%, p = 0.0135).
evidence.sample_unit: benchmark items (100 clinical vignettes and 150 internal medicine exam questions)

evidence.title: Immersive, Interactive, Intelligent Patient Educational System for Venous Thromboembolism (ChatVTE): Development and Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Expert Likert ratings of accuracy, completeness, consistency, and safety: retrieval-augmented ChatVTE vs ChatGPT
evidence.effect: ChatVTE outperformed ChatGPT on accuracy, completeness, consistency (all P<.001, r>0.5) and safety (P=.01, r=0.327). The comparison is confounded, since the two systems differ in model as well as retrieval.
evidence.quote: Expert evaluation demonstrated that ChatVTE significantly outperformed ChatGPT in accuracy, completeness, consistency (all P<.001, r>0.5), and safety (P=.01, r=0.327).

evidence.title: A Guideline-Concordant Chatbot Framework for Structured Colorectal Cancer Screening: Multistage Feasibility Study
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated dialogue quality with guideline knowledge base (V2/V3) vs role-only prompt (V1)
evidence.effect: V3 (knowledge base plus structured prompt) scored higher than V1 across all 6 dimensions (adjusted P<.05); Kruskal-Wallis all P<.001. Knowledge base confounded with slot-filling and formatting changes.
evidence.quote: Post hoc analyses using Dunn test with Bonferroni correction showed that prompt V3 scored higher than prompt V1 across all dimensions (adjusted P <.05).

evidence.title: Development and Usability Assessment of a Health Education Conversational Agent for Patients With Gastric Cancer: Action Research Study
evidence.outcome: Answer accuracy and RAG knowledge hit rate across three alpha-testing rounds
evidence.effect: Accuracy 67% (37/55), 71% (44/62), 82% (31/38); RAG knowledge hit rates 86%, 98%, 100%; hit-rate differences significant (P<.01). No non-RAG comparator.
evidence.quote: The accuracy of the agent in 3 rounds was 67% (37/55), 71% (44/62), and 82% (31/38), respectively; RAG knowledge hit rates reached 86% (47/55), 98% (61/62), and 100% (38/38).
evidence.sample_unit: participants (44 patients, 13 nurses, 3 nursing managers, 2 surgeons, 1 psychologist, 1 dietitian)

evidence.title: MedPAO: A Protocol-Driven Agent for Structuring Medical Reports
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated quality of structured CXR report outputs, protocol-grounded agent versus LLM-only baselines
evidence.effect: Expert radiologists and clinicians rated outputs 4.52 out of 5 on average; concept categorization F1 was 0.96; reported as surpassing LLM-only foundation-model baselines.
evidence.quote: Notably, expert radiologists and clinicians rated the final structured outputs with an average score of 4.52 out of 5, indicating a level of reliability that surpasses baseline approaches relying solely on LLM-based foundation models.

evidence.title: Rethinking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine: A Large-Scale, Systematic Expert Evaluation and Practical Insights
evidence.outcome: Factuality and completeness of RAG vs non-RAG LLM responses, expert-rated
evidence.effect: Standard RAG often degraded performance: factuality and completeness dropped by up to 6% and 5% versus non-RAG; only 22% of top-16 passages relevant; evidence selection precision 41-43%, recall 27-49%.
evidence.quote: Contrary to expectation, standard RAG often degraded performance: only 22% of top-16 passages were relevant, evidence selection remained weak (precision 41-43%, recall 27-49%), and factuality and completeness dropped by up to 6% and 5%, respectively, compared with non-RAG variants.
evidence.sample_unit: model outputs annotated by 18 medical experts (80,502 annotations; 200 queries)

evidence.title: COMPARE: Clinical Optimization with Modular Planning and Assessment via RAG-Enhanced AI-OCT: Superior Decision Support for Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Compared to ChatGPT-5 and Junior Operators
evidence.outcome: Agreement of PCI planning decisions with expert record, RAG-enhanced CA-GPT versus general ChatGPT-5
evidence.effect: Pre-PCI median agreement score 5 (IQR 3.75-5) for CA-GPT vs 3 (2-4) for ChatGPT-5 (P<0.001); post-PCI 5 (4.75-5) vs 4 (4-5) (P<0.001).
evidence.quote: For pre-PCI planning, CA-GPT demonstrated significantly higher median agreement scores (5[IQR 3.75-5]) compared to both ChatGPT-5 (3[2-4], P<0.001) and junior physicians (4[3-4], P<0.001).

evidence.title: Enhancing Mental Health Counseling Support in Bangladesh using Culturally-Grounded Knowledge
evidence.outcome: Counseling response quality with clinically validated knowledge graph grounding versus RAG alone
evidence.effect: KG-based approaches consistently improved contextual relevance, clinical appropriateness, and practical usability compared to RAG alone (no numbers in abstract).
evidence.quote: The results show that KG-based approaches consistently improve contextual relevance, clinical appropriateness, and practical usability compared to RAG alone, demonstrating that structured, expert-validated knowledge plays a critical role in addressing LLMs limitations in counseling tasks.

evidence.title: The Provenance Gap in Clinical AI: Evidence-Traceable Temporal Knowledge Graphs for Rare Disease Reasoning
evidence.outcome: Evidence verifiability and clinical coverage of grounded knowledge graph versus ungrounded/RAG baselines
evidence.effect: HEG-TKG matched baseline clinical feature coverage with 100% evidence verifiability (203 inline citations); Guideline-RAG produced zero verifiable citations; clinician evaluation d = 1.81, p < 0.001, no degradation on safety or completeness.
evidence.quote: In a controlled three-arm comparison using the same synthesis model, HEG-TKG matches baseline clinical feature coverage while achieving 100% evidence verifiability with 203 inline citations.

evidence.title: Can Language Models Identify Side Effects of Breast Cancer Radiation Treatments?
evidence.outcome: Reliability and robustness of LLM side effect lists with grounding in clinician-curated lists
evidence.effect: Grounding outputs in clinician-curated side effect lists substantially improved reliability and robustness; numeric constraints alone reduced precision (no numbers in abstract).
evidence.quote: When used alone, constraints on the number of side effects generated reduce precision, and grounding outputs in clinician-curated side effect lists substantially improves reliability and robustness.
evidence.sample_unit: breast cancer patient profiles (paired scenarios differing in radiotherapy regimen)

evidence.title: Evidence-Based Intelligent Diagnostic and Therapeutic Visualization System with Large Language Models: Multi-Turn Interaction and Multimodal Treatment Plan Generation
evidence.outcome: Non-standard outputs with versus without knowledge graph constraints
evidence.effect: Knowledge graph constraints reduced non-standard outputs by 32%.
evidence.quote: Knowledge graph constraints reduced non-standard outputs by 32%.

evidence.title: TTFT-Aware Graph Chain-of-Thought:Distance-Indexed Neural A* for Low-Hallucination Multi-Hop Medical Reasoning
evidence.outcome: Clinician-audited hallucinations, latency, and recall for graph-path-grounded generation versus text-only RAG
evidence.effect: Hybrid PLL+AStarNet graph-grounded generation gave a better latency/recall Pareto frontier than text-only RAG, lowered TTFT, and reduced clinician-audited hallucinations; no numbers reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: On fertility-focused queries, the hybrid (PLL+AStarNet) establishes a better latency/recall Pareto frontier than text-only RAG and single-component baselines, lowers TTFT, and reduces clinician-audited hallucinations while preserving explanation clarity.

evidence.title: Medi-Gemma: A Hybrid Clinical Decision Support System Integrating Deterministic EMR Analytics and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
evidence.outcome: Factual adherence and context drift of LLM outputs when grounded in structured EMR data and RAG
evidence.effect: Abstract reports the architecture eliminates semantic context drift, prevents database compilation crashes, and improves factual adherence to backend clinical repositories. No numeric results are given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Validation shows that this architecture eliminates semantic context drift, prevents database compilation crashes, and improves factual adherence to backend clinical repositories.

evidence.title: A safety-oriented hypothetico-deductive framework for AI-assisted differential diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Top-3 diagnostic accuracy with evidence-grounded verification framework versus standalone LLM on case reports
evidence.effect: Top-3 accuracy 59.9% vs 52.1% (JAMA) and 62.7% vs 51.4% (NEJM); Annals of Emergency Medicine 85.7% vs 68.6%.
evidence.quote: On literature-derived case reports from NEJM and JAMA, with GPT-oss-120B as the shared backbone, Top-3 diagnostic accuracy was 59.9% versus 52.1% for the standalone LLM on JAMA cases and 62.7% versus 51.4% on NEJM cases.
evidence.sample_unit: real-world emergency department notes (blinded physician evaluation)

evidence.title: Designing Safety-Constrained LLM Systems for Public Health Information Access
evidence.outcome: Grounding of responses in curated public health resources via domain-restricted RAG
evidence.effect: Scenario validation reported reliable resource grounding; no quantitative grounding metric or comparison reported in abstract.
evidence.quote: Results show consistent enforcement of safety constraints, reliable resource grounding, and stable system performance, with an average response time of 5.3 seconds.

evidence.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation in LLMs for Mental Health: Quantifying the Incremental Contribution of Retrieval Within a Layered Safety Architecture
evidence.outcome: Intent classification accuracy/recall for RAG-enabled versus RAG-disabled LLM modes in mental health chatbot
evidence.effect: RAG improved accuracy, consistency and safety of intent detection, with a rise in false alarms; routed to additional review.
evidence.quote: While RAG caused a rise in false alarms, the trade-off is consistent with safety-critical design principles that prioritize sensitivity, where flagged cases are routed to additional review rather than acted on directly.

evidence.title: Anchoring Clinical Events in Time: UID-Preserving Multimodal Reconstruction and Source-Grounded Adjudication
evidence.outcome: Temporal agreement and event recovery with versus without structured-evidence source-row grounding
evidence.effect: GLM 5.2 multimodal revision improved temporal agreement over text-only without reducing event recovery; adjudication favored multimodal for GLM 5.2 but not DeepSeek V3.2; other models showed smaller gains.
evidence.quote: Ablations showed that UIDs primarily preserve event retention, whereas source-row linkage supports temporal placement.

evidence.title: Medical Knowledge Is Not All You Need: When Medical Q&A Becomes Situated Patient Assistance
evidence.outcome: effect of procedural grounding
evidence.effect: Errors remained substantial; with full procedural context, six of seven models more often introduced later steps prematurely.
evidence.quote: Errors remained substantial, including treating unknown states as known, even under explicit guardrails; with full procedural context, six of seven models more often introduced later steps prematurely.

evidence.title: Optimizing the Clinical Application of Rheumatology Guidelines Using Large Language Models: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework Integrating EULAR and ACR Recommendations
evidence.outcome: Answer quality (accuracy, safety, completeness) of RAG-grounded versus baseline LLM answers to guideline questions
evidence.effect: RAG significantly outperformed baseline across all criteria (p<0.001) per LLM judge; rheumatologists confirmed for accuracy, safety, completeness (p<0.001); RAG preferred in 92.8% of LLM-judge and 71.2%-74.8% of human comparisons.
evidence.quote: Analysis revealed that the RAG system significantly outperformed the baseline system across all criteria (p<0.001) in the LLM-as-a-judge evaluation.

evidence.title: OncoGPT: A Modular AI Assistant Orchestrating LLMs in Molecular Oncology
evidence.outcome: Expert acceptance of context-grounded LLM outputs on oncology report prompts
evidence.effect: Automatic model selection with context achieved expert acceptance across all 19 prompts; a fixed high-end model had higher cost and lower expert-rated quality. No comparison without context was reported.
evidence.quote: Evaluated on 19 representative clinical prompts derived from real-world oncology reports, automatic model selection with context achieved expert acceptance across all prompts while reducing inference cost by an order of magnitude; by contrast, a fixed high-end model produced higher cost and lower expert-rated quality.

evidence.title: Multi-Modal Large Language Model for Medical Auxiliary Diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Ablation of retrieval and knowledge modules on expert-rated accuracy, treatment relevance, and reliability
evidence.effect: Abstract reports superior accuracy, treatment relevance, and information reliability versus general-purpose models, and that ablations show each module is essential. No numbers reported in the text.
evidence.quote: Ablation studies highlight the essential role of each module, particularly in managing multi-modal information.

evidence.title: Development and validation of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and GraphRAG for complex clinical cases
evidence.outcome: Clinical correctness and guideline adherence of RAG versus baseline LLM
evidence.effect: RAG-based methods outperformed the baseline LLM in clinical correctness and guideline adherence; GraphRAG achieved highest patient-specificity but lower clarity.
evidence.quote: RAG-based methods outperformed the baseline LLM in clinical correctness and guideline adherence.

evidence.title: Systematic Evaluation of Multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Gastrointestinal Tumor Board Decision Support
evidence.outcome: Concordance with multidisciplinary team recommendations with vs without curated guideline retrieval and query rewriting
evidence.effect: Baseline concordance 79–85%; query rewriting plus curated guideline retrieval improved concordance to 93–95% (p < 0.01).
evidence.quote: Combining query rewriting with curated guideline retrieval improved concordance to 93–95% (p < 0.01), with prompt design and corpus curation exerting greater influence than model selection.

evidence.title: EndoBot: An LLM Workflow-Driven Agent for Intelligent Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Consultation
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and safety of GI endoscopy consultation, RAG-grounded agent versus standalone LLM
evidence.effect: Abstract reports RAG-enhanced agent significantly improved accuracy and safety versus standalone LLMs; no numbers given. Challenges persist in edge cases and non-Chinese inquiries.
evidence.quote: This study demonstrates that RAG-enhanced Agent significantly improve the accuracy and safety of AI-driven GI endoscopy consultations compared to standalone LLMs.

evidence.title: Asymmetric sociodemographic disparity in evidence-grounded clinical AI
evidence.outcome: Whether literature-grounded output removes sociodemographic disparity
evidence.effect: Literature grounding did not remove disparity; authors state it may redistribute sociodemographic disparity rather than remove it.
evidence.quote: Literature grounding may redistribute sociodemographic disparity in clinical AI rather than remove it.
evidence.sample_unit: emergency-department cases (each varied across 20 sociodemographic labels)

evidence.title: Evidence-Graded Decision Authorization for Safe Clinical AI: A Constrained Reasoning Framework
evidence.outcome: unjustified inference and appropriate refusal
evidence.effect: RAG 47.7% vs 48.7% unjustified inference, p = 0.870; appropriate refusal 56.9% vs 56.9%, p = 1.0.
evidence.quote: An unexpected finding was that retrieval-augmented generation without an authorization gate failed to reduce unjustified inference relative to the unconstrained baseline (47.7% vs. 48.7%, p = 0.870) and produced no improvement in appropriate refusal (56.9% vs. 56.9%, p = 1.0), showing that information supply alone is not sufficient for inferential governance.

evidence.title: Multi-Agent AI for Chest Radiography: A Sequential Segmentation and LLM-Driven Consultative Tool for Medical Training
evidence.outcome: Visual hallucination in LLM consultation when grounded in segmentation outputs and blocking unanchored queries
evidence.effect: Authors report the system eliminates visual hallucinations by intercepting unanchored queries; no quantitative results or comparator reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: The system effectively eliminates visual hallucinations by intercepting unanchored queries.

evidence.title: Don’t stop the heart: a performance analysis of large language models and potassium dosing
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and errors with versus without clinician-curated dosing guideline provided to model
evidence.effect: Total errors dropped from 165 to 104; accuracy improved from 45% to 65%; severity of potential harm reduced with guidance, though still considerable.
evidence.quote: When given the potassium dosing guideline, total errors dropped from 165 to 104, and average accuracy improved from 45% to 65% with GPT-5-Chat.
evidence.sample_unit: clinician-annotated hypokalemia cases (each run in triplicate)

evidence.title: Implementing Generative Artificial Intelligence in a Tertiary Hospital Health Screening Center
evidence.outcome: Completeness, safety, and preference of RAG chatbot versus general-purpose AI models
evidence.effect: Institution-specific RAG chatbot outperformed general-purpose AI models in completeness, safety, and overall preference; favorable preliminary usability (numbers not reported in abstract).
evidence.quote: An institution-specific retrieval-augmented generation chatbot showed favorable preliminary usability and outperformed general-purpose AI models in completeness, safety, and overall preference.

evidence.title: First the Rules, Then the Summary: Piloting a Design for Accurate LLM-Generated Clinical Summaries
evidence.outcome: Substantive numerical/categorical errors in constrained pipeline versus unconstrained LLM summaries
evidence.effect: Harness found one substantive content error (0.05%) across 2,067 checks in constrained pipeline, versus about two in five checkable numerical statements wrong in unconstrained baseline.
evidence.quote: Across the three models (Gemma 4 31B, Gemini 3 Flash, GPT-4.1), the harness identified one substantive content error, meaning one that would change a clinician’s reading, for a rate of 0.05%, against an unconstrained baseline in which about two in five checkable numerical statements were wrong.

evidence.title: AI as a signal assessor – Can a Large Language Model perform causality assessment on a case series?
evidence.outcome: Effect of prompt design (case series data, anti-hallucination instructions) on output grounding
evidence.effect: Providing Bradford Hill descriptions, including case series data, and adding explicit anti-hallucination instructions improved specificity and grounding; annotators agreed with 79–92% of output sentences.
evidence.quote: Prompt design substantially influenced output quality; providing Bradford Hill viewpoint descriptions, including case series data, and adding explicit anti-hallucination instructions improved specificity and grounding.

evidence.title: Comparing Physicians’ Assessments of Context-specific AI-powered clinical reasoning assistant with General-Purpose AI agent: A Prospective Multi-Site Physician Evaluation of VITA versus ChatGPT in India and Bangladesh
evidence.outcome: Physician-rated evidence quality of retrieval-augmented context-specific AI versus general-purpose AI
evidence.effect: Evidence quality VITA 4.46 vs ChatGPT 3.14 (42% relative gap); composite 25.4 vs 22.3 (+3.1, t = 8.31, p < 0.001). Retrieval augmentation was bundled with local context, so its effect is not isolated.
evidence.quote: The largest advantage was in evidence quality (VITA: 4.46 vs. ChatGPT: 3.14, a 42% relative gap).
evidence.sample_unit: observations (physician ratings across 6 dimensions of AI responses to hypothetical case vignettes; 37 physicians)

evidence.title: Representation Before Retrieval: Structured Patient Artifacts Reduce Hallucination in Clinical AI Systems
evidence.outcome: Unsupported claim rate with RAG over raw clinical text versus baseline LLM
evidence.effect: Unsupported claims rose from 5.0% (95% CI 3.8–6.4%) at baseline to 43.6% (95% CI 40.1–47.2%) with retrieval, an 8.7-fold increase (p<0.001, d=2.31).
evidence.quote: RAG substantially increased hallucination: unsupported claim rates rose from 5.0% (95% CI: 3.8–6.4%) at baseline to 43.6% (95% CI: 40.1–47.2%) with retrieval—an 8.7-fold increase (  p < 0.001, Cohen’s  d = 2.31).
evidence.sample_unit: generated outputs (100 synthetic vignettes x 3 seeds x 4 conditions)

evidence.title: A Chatbot for the Management of Bipolar Disorder: Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation with an Open-Weight Large Language Model to Answer Clinical Questions Based on the CANMAT and ISBD 2018 Guidelines for Bipolar Disorder
evidence.outcome: Guideline consistency of chatbot answers, RAG versus base LLM, rated by expert psychiatrists
evidence.effect: RAG: 80 (63.5%) fully consistent vs 24 (19.0%) baseline; major deviation 10 (7.9%) vs 48 (38.1%); OR = 9.1, 95% CI 5.3–16.3, p < 0.001.
evidence.quote: The RAG system produced 80 answers (63.5%) rated fully consistent with the guidelines versus 24 (19.0%) for baseline, and only 10 answers with major deviation (7.9%) versus 48 (38.1%) for baseline.

evidence.title: Toward Trustworthy Chatbots: A Protocol for Red Teaming for Health Related Conversations
evidence.outcome: document augmentation for grounded responses
evidence.effect: Document augmentation eliminated user_distress errors to 0/20 and reduced advice_query errors 7/20→4/20.
evidence.quote: Document augmentation eliminated all single-turn user_distress errors (to 0/20) and reduced advice_query errors (7/20→4/20).

evidence.title: Hippocrates-o1  : A Guideline-Aware, Orchestrated, Self-Refining Protocol for Specialty-Specific Clinical Reasoning
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated hallucination audit and reasoning scores, guideline-informed retrieval pipeline versus vanilla LLM
evidence.effect: Hallucination Audit rose from 3.90±1.32 to 4.74±0.76; Overall Reasoning rose from 3.40±0.90 to 4.00±0.73 (p<0.001). Effect is confounded with structured prompts and self-refinement.
evidence.quote: Domain scores increased for Clinical Knowledge Application (2.87±1.20 to 3.70±1.03), Contextual Understanding (3.48±0.95 to 3.98±0.95), Hallucination Audit (3.90±1.32 to 4.74±0.76), Reasoning Transparency (3.45±1.02 to 3.86±0.87), and Chain-of-Thought Quality (3.32±1.04 to 3.69±1.00), all p≤0.001.
evidence.sample_unit: patient cases (head and neck cancer notes from MIMIC-IV-Note)

evidence.title: Blinded Expert Evaluation of Large Language Models for Osteoporosis Case Management in Older Adults: Impact of Direct Guideline Integration
evidence.outcome: Quality scores of LLMs with versus without guideline document integration
evidence.effect: Base ChatGPT 4.5 scored 22.76/25 vs 21.42 for guideline-loaded ChatGPT 4.5 and 21.56 for NotebookLM + guideline; base model significantly superior to three panels; differences in accuracy (p=0.0006) and guideline compliance (p<0.0001).
evidence.quote: the lack of benefit from guideline uploading suggests unstructured presentation may be inadequate for integration.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (25 hypothetical cases x 4 panels)

evidence.title: Multi-Agent Dynamic Refinement Outperforms Static RAG in Clinical Reasoning for Complex Nephrology Cases
evidence.outcome: Human-rated clinical reasoning score (20-point) with static guideline RAG versus baseline LLM
evidence.effect: Static RAG (Model B, mean 16.2, SD 1.2) yielded no significant improvement over baseline Model A (16.1, 1.3); multi-agent RAG with self-critique (Model C) scored 17.2 (P < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Implementing static RAG (Model B) yielded no significant improvement over the baseline.

evidence.title: CardioAgent: A Traceable Agentic and Retrieval-Augmented Architecture for Cardiovascular Clinical Decision Support
evidence.outcome: Weighted accuracy across generic LLM, domain-prompted LLM, and full agent with guideline RAG and tools
evidence.effect: Weighted accuracy rose from 55.6% (generic LLM) to 66.7% (domain prompting) to 100% (full agent) on 9 synthetic cases; Wilson 95% CI 70.1–100%. Small synthetic set, keyword scoring, no cardiologist adjudication.
evidence.quote: In a controlled set of nine synthetic cardiovascular cases, weighted accuracy increased from 55.6% for the generic LLM to 66.7% after domain prompting and to 100% with the complete agent.

evidence.title: Ensuring Inferential Reliability in Clinical LLMs: A Proof-Theoretic Approach via the ISA System
evidence.outcome: Student ratings of rigor, transparency, reliability, and safety for knowledge-base-constrained vs unconstrained LLM
evidence.effect: Participants rated the constrained system, whose derivations are limited to a drug-leaflet knowledge base, more highly than unconstrained conversational systems on inferential rigor, transparency, clinical reliability, and perceived safety.
evidence.quote: Participants consistently rated the constrained system more highly with respect to inferential rigor, transparency, clinical reliability, and perceived safety.

evidence.title: MTS-Bench: A Manchester Triage System Benchmark for Language Model Triage Safety
evidence.outcome: Undertriage rate of retrieval-grounded agentic system versus general-purpose LLM
evidence.effect: Undertriage was 11.5% for both DR. INFO configurations versus 44.2% for GPT-5.1 (Fisher's exact p = 1.0 x 10^-10).
evidence.quote: On this benchmark, replacing a general purpose language model with an agentic retrieval augmented system over a curated clinical knowledge base substantially reduced the undertriage rate.
evidence.sample_unit: prompts per system (39 cases x 4 permutations x with/without anchoring statement)

evidence.title: Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models for Clinically Aligned Adverse Event Coding in Acute Myeloid Leukemia Clinical Trials
evidence.outcome: MedDRA coding accuracy of retrieval-grounded LLM versus zero-shot generation and random candidate selection
evidence.effect: RAG pipeline reached LLT exact accuracy 50-58%, PT 78-85%, SOC 90-93%, and expert clinical acceptability 91-97%; zero-shot and random selection performed substantially worse.
evidence.quote: Zero-shot generation and random candidate selection performed substantially worse.

evidence.title: Diagnostic Accuracy Masks Outdated Reasoning: Evaluating LLMs on Evolving Clinical Guidelines
evidence.outcome: Superseded-vocabulary use with guideline corpus context versus no-context baseline
evidence.effect: Injecting guideline context of any kind increased superseded-vocabulary use for every model relative to the no-context baseline.
evidence.quote: First, injecting guideline context of any kind increased superseded-vocabulary use for every model relative to the no-context baseline.

evidence.title: Almanac: Retrieval-Augmented Language Models for Clinical Medicine
evidence.outcome: Physician-rated factuality of retrieval-augmented LLM versus standard LLMs on clinical scenarios
evidence.effect: Significant increases in factuality (mean of 18% at p-value < 0.05) across all specialties, with improvements in completeness and safety.
evidence.quote: Performance on a novel dataset of clinical scenarios (n = 130) evaluated by a panel of 5 board-certified and resident physicians demonstrates significant increases in factuality (mean of 18% at p-value < 0.05) across all specialties, with improvements in completeness and safety.

evidence.title: ChatGPT in Occupational Medicine: A Comparative Study with Human Experts
evidence.outcome: completeness with legislative context

evidence.title: ChatGPT-CARE: a Superior Decision Support Tool Enhancing ChatGPT with Clinical Practice Guidelines
evidence.outcome: accuracy, hallucination, and clarity
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-CARE showed increased accuracy and clarity, with moderate hallucination, versus original ChatGPT.
evidence.quote: The results indicate that ChatGPT-CARE offers increased accuracy and clarity, with moderate hallucination, compared to the original ChatGPT.

evidence.title: Large Language Models and Medical Knowledge Grounding for Diagnosis Prediction
evidence.outcome: Diagnosis prediction and rationale quality when LLMs are grounded in a medical knowledge graph via RAG
evidence.effect: Abstract reports no numeric results; it describes both challenges and opportunities in using external knowledge graph grounding for diagnosis prediction.
evidence.quote: Using real-world hospital datasets, our study serves to enrich the discourse on the role of medical KGs in grounding medical knowledge into LLMs, revealing both challenges and opportunities in harnessing external knowledge for explainable diagnostic pathway and the realization of AI-augmented diagnostic decision support systems.

evidence.title: Empowering Personalized Pharmacogenomics with Generative AI Solutions
evidence.outcome: AI assistant performance on PGx question catalog, RAG-grounded GPT-4 versus ChatGPT 3.5
evidence.effect: RAG-based GPT-4 assistant performed better than ChatGPT 3.5, especially on provider-specific queries requiring specialized data and citations; no numeric results reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Compared with OpenAI’s ChatGPT 3.5, it demonstrated better performance, especially in provider-specific queries requiring specialized data and citations.

evidence.title: Development and Testing of a Novel Large Language Model-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems for Medication Safety in 12 Clinical Specialties
evidence.outcome: DRP detection performance of RAG-LLM versus LLM alone
evidence.effect: RAG-LLM performed better than LLM alone; DRP detection accuracy improved in several categories but at the expense of lower precision.
evidence.quote: RAG-LLM performed better compared to LLM alone.
evidence.sample_unit: prescribing error scenarios embedded in 23 clinical vignettes

evidence.title: Mitigating Hallucinations in Large Language Models: A Comparative Study of RAG-enhanced vs. Human-Generated Medical Templates
evidence.outcome: Physician-rated accuracy and usefulness of RAG-grounded LLM templates versus human-generated templates
evidence.effect: LLM templates grounded in clinical guidelines scored higher on average for accuracy and usefulness than human templates; BERTScore showed high textual similarity. No non-RAG LLM comparator, no numbers in abstract.
evidence.quote: The LLM templates scored higher on average for both accuracy and usefulness when compared to human-generated templates.

evidence.title: Reducing Surgeons’ Routine Task Burden, Enhancing Surgical Decision Making, and Ensuring Patient Safety Using SurgeryLLM
evidence.outcome: Whether RAG output incorporated evidence-based surgical guideline knowledge for patient-specific data
evidence.effect: Abstract reports SurgeryLLM demonstrably incorporated domain-specific knowledge from current evidence-based surgical guidelines; no numeric results are given in the text.
evidence.quote: SurgeryLLM, a large language model framework using Retrieval Augmented Generation demonstrably incorporated domain-specific knowledge from current evidence-based surgical guidelines when presented with patient-specific data.

evidence.title: Biological Database Mining for LLM-Driven Alzheimer’s Disease Drug Repurposing
evidence.outcome: Hallucination rate of LLM drug repurposing responses, ontology/knowledge-graph prompt versus zero-shot control
evidence.effect: Ontology-based prompt produced fewer hallucinations than zero-shot control in a manual hallucination check; the abstract gives no numeric rates.
evidence.quote: The results of the ontology-based prompt showed fewer hallucinations in their responses compared to the zero-shot control prompting.

evidence.title: ChatGPT on guidelines: Providing contextual knowledge to GPT allows it to provide advice on appropriate colonoscopy intervals
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of colonoscopy interval advice, standard GPT-4 versus guideline-contextualized GPT-4
evidence.effect: The contextualized GPT4 model outperformed the standard GPT4 in all domains. No high-risk features were missed, and only two cases had hallucination of additional high-risk features.
evidence.quote: The contextualized GPT4 model outperformed the standard GPT4 in all domains.

evidence.title: A Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT)-Powered Chatbot as a Simulated Patient to Practice History Taking: Prospective, Mixed Methods Study
evidence.outcome: Share of GPT answers based on script information versus fictitious information
evidence.effect: Script-covered questions (n=502): 94.4% (n=471) answers based on explicit script information. Questions not covered (n=195): 56.4% (n=110) of answers used fictitious information.
evidence.quote: When questions were explicitly covered by the script (n=502, 60.3%), the GPT-provided answers were mostly based on explicit script information (n=471, 94.4%).

evidence.title: Development of a liver disease-specific large language model chat interface using retrieval-augmented generation
evidence.outcome: Hepatologist ratings of accuracy, comprehensiveness and safety of RAG-grounded LLM versus ungrounded LLMs
evidence.effect: LiVersa (RAG on 30 AASLD documents) was more accurate but rated less comprehensive and safe than ChatGPT 4; it answered all 10 trainee knowledge-assessment questions correctly.
evidence.quote: LiVersa's outputs were more accurate but were rated less comprehensive and safe compared to those of ChatGPT 4.

evidence.title: Clinical decision support for bipolar depression using large language models
evidence.venue: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology
evidence.outcome: Rate of selecting expert-defined optimal treatment with vs without guideline grounding in prompt
evidence.effect: Augmented model chose optimal treatment for 50.8% vs 23.4% for un-augmented model (McNemar's p<0.001); kappa 0.31 vs 0.09.
evidence.quote: For 234 (23.4%) of vignettes, the model identified the optimal treatment, a result significantly poorer than for the augmented model (McNemar’s p < 0.001)

evidence.title: Optimization of hepatological clinical guidelines interpretation by large language models: a retrieval augmented generation-based framework
evidence.outcome: LLM answer accuracy on hepatitis C guideline questions with vs without guideline context (RAG)
evidence.effect: Accuracy rose from 43% to 99% (p < 0.001) when guidelines were provided as context in a coherent text corpus with non-text sources converted to text.
evidence.quote: The results showed a significant improvement in accuracy from 43 to 99% (p < 0.001), when guidelines were provided as context in a coherent corpus of text and non-text sources were converted into text.

evidence.title: Building Trustworthy Generative Artificial Intelligence for Diabetes Care and Limb Preservation: A Medical Knowledge Extraction Case
evidence.venue: Journal of diabetes science and technology
evidence.outcome: Expert-reviewed accuracy of RAG-grounded GPT-4 answers to diabetes and diabetic foot care questions
evidence.effect: RAG model grounded in a curated knowledge base (295 articles) achieved 98% accuracy on 175 questions with appropriate content volume and few-shot prompts; no non-RAG comparator reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: The study demonstrated that with appropriate content volume and few-shot learning prompts, the RAG model achieved 98% accuracy, confirming its capability to offer user-friendly and comprehensible medical information.

evidence.title: Applying generative AI with retrieval augmented generation to summarize and extract key clinical information from electronic health records
evidence.outcome: Summarization accuracy with versus without RAG grounding; hallucination mitigation
evidence.effect: Zero-shot summaries had 93.25% accuracy; adding RAG gave a 6% increase to 99.25% accuracy. RAG did not further improve accuracy in the risk factor extraction task (about 90%).
evidence.quote: The addition of RAG improved the summarization process, leading to a 6% increase and achieving an accuracy of 99.25%.
evidence.sample_unit: notes (25 for summarization task; 1,399 for extraction task)

evidence.title: Generating colloquial radiology reports with large language models
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM colloquial radiology translations with vs without extracted medical term definitions in prompt
evidence.effect: Across all grade levels, the approach was 20% more accurate than baseline; 88% (Findings) and 93% (Impression) accuracy at 8th-grade level.
evidence.quote: Across all grade levels, our approach was 20% more accurate than the baseline method.

evidence.title: A Blinded Comparison of Three Generative Artificial Intelligence Chatbots for Orthopaedic Surgery Therapeutic Questions
evidence.outcome: Blinded expert preference and rubric scores for a retrieval-based chatbot versus general chatbots
evidence.effect: AskOE was preferred over ChatGPT (P<0.001) and Bing (P<0.001) and had significantly higher total evaluation scores than both (P<0.001).
evidence.quote: Across all questions and answers, AskOE was preferred by reviewers to a significantly greater extent than both ChatGPT (P<0.001) and Bing (P<0.001).

evidence.title: Expert-Guided Large Language Models for Clinical Decision Support in Precision Oncology
evidence.outcome: Semantic similarity to tumor board recommendations, draft (PubMed only) versus enhanced system with curated evidence sources
evidence.effect: Semantic similarity rose from 0.71 to 0.76 (P = .01); concordance with expert recommendations was 94.7% for the enhanced system; median 4 options vs 2 for the MTB.
evidence.quote: This broader approach was achieved by incorporating a curated medical data set that contextualized molecular targetability.

evidence.title: Application of NotebookLM, a large language model with retrieval-augmented generation, for lung cancer staging
evidence.outcome: Lung cancer staging accuracy with RAG grounding versus GPT-4o with and without reference knowledge
evidence.effect: NotebookLM (RAG) 86% accuracy vs GPT-4o 39% with REK in prompt and 25% without REK.
evidence.quote: NotebookLM achieved 86% diagnostic accuracy in the lung cancer staging experiment, outperforming GPT-4o, which recorded 39% accuracy with the REK and 25% without it.

evidence.title: EyeGPT for Patient Inquiries and Medical Education: Development and Validation of an Ophthalmology Large Language Model
evidence.outcome: Hallucination proportion and response score with vs without retrieval grounding in ophthalmology textbooks
evidence.effect: Adding book retrieval improved score (mean 13.08 vs 15.14; P=.001) and reduced hallucinations (71/120, 59.2% vs 57/120, 47.4%, P=.02) versus fine-tuned model alone.
evidence.quote: Incorporating information retrieval from reliable sources, particularly ophthalmology textbooks, further improved the model's response compared with solely the best fine-tuned model (mean 13.08, SD 5.43 vs mean 15.14, SD 4.64; P=.001) and reduced hallucinations (71/120, 59.2% vs 57/120, 47.4%, P=.02).

evidence.title: Evaluating Artificial Intelligence-Driven Responses to Acute Liver Failure Queries: A Comparative Analysis Across Accuracy, Clarity, and Relevance
evidence.outcome: Likert accuracy, clarity, relevance of GPT-4 with RAG versus other LLMs on ALF queries
evidence.effect: GPT-4 with RAG scored highest across accuracy, clarity, relevance (4.70, 4.89, 4.78) versus GPT-4 without RAG (3.67 accuracy, 4.04 clarity, 4.01 relevance).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT 4, augmented with RAG, demonstrated superior performance compared with others, consistently scoring the highest (4.70, 4.89, 4.78) across all 3 domains.

evidence.title: Evaluation of the integration of retrieval-augmented generation in large language model for breast cancer nursing care responses
evidence.outcome: Nurse-rated accuracy of answers to breast cancer nursing questions, RAG-GPT versus GPT-4 alone
evidence.effect: Accuracy 8.6 ± 0.69 with RAG vs 5.6 ± 0.96 with GPT-4 alone, p < 0.01; satisfaction 8.4 vs 5.4, p < 0.01.
evidence.quote: The RAG-GPT model demonstrated a significantly higher accuracy after integrating the local knowledge base data than the GPT-4 group (8.6 ± 0.69 vs. 5.6 ± 0.96, p < 0.01).

evidence.title: Empowering PET imaging reporting with retrieval-augmented large language models and reading reports database: a pilot single center study
evidence.venue: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
evidence.outcome: Appropriateness score of suggested diagnoses, RAG LLM versus LLM without RAG, rated by nuclear medicine physicians
evidence.effect: Appropriateness score of suggested potential diagnoses was significantly better with the RAG system than with the LLM without RAG; 84.1% of cases retrieved relevant similar cases per all three readers.
evidence.quote: Using the RAG system, the appropriateness score of the suggested potential diagnoses was significantly better than that of the LLM without RAG.

evidence.title: Smart Pharmaceutical Monitoring System With Personalized Medication Schedules and Self-Management Programs for Patients With Diabetes: Development and Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated medication schedule accuracy and safety: evidence-database-constrained system vs ungrounded GPT-4
evidence.effect: DUMS vs GPT-4 accuracy 4.43 vs 3.84 and safety 4.44 vs 3.91 (both P<.001); total score 37.96 vs 36.35 (P<.001).
evidence.quote: The evaluation results revealed that the DUMS group achieved significantly higher accuracy and safety scores than the GPT-4 group ( P <.001), with full consideration of multiple aspects of DDI, pharmacokinetics, and dietary restrictions.
evidence.sample_unit: prescriptions of older patients with diabetes (60 medication plans rated by 12 specialists)

evidence.title: Potential role of ChatGPT in simplifying and improving informed consent forms for vaccination: a pilot study conducted in Italy
evidence.outcome: Clinician ratings of consent forms
evidence.effect: C (ChatGPT rephrasing A) vs B (AI-only): adequacy median 4.0 vs 3.0; overall judgement 3.0 vs 2.0; B-C differences p<0.01 and p=0.002.
evidence.quote: Consent form B, generated entirely by ChatGPT, scored lower, suggesting that collaboration between AI and humans yields better results: ChatGPT alone might not be sufficient to produce the best and most accepted product, and that the best results are achieved through the collaborative use of LLMs and human expertise.

evidence.title: Evaluating Adherence to Canadian Radiology Guidelines for Incidental Hepatobiliary Findings Using RAG-Enabled LLMs
evidence.venue: Canadian Association of Radiologists journal = Journal l'Association canadienne des radiologistes
evidence.outcome: Guideline adherence of LLM outputs with vs without RAG grounding
evidence.effect: Adherence 81.7% GPT-4o without RAG vs 97.2% with RAG; 79.3% o1-mini without RAG vs 95.1% with RAG (P < .05).
evidence.quote: Adherence rates were 81.7% for GPT-4o without RAG, 97.2% for GPT-4o with RAG, 79.3% for o1-mini without RAG, and 95.1% for o1-mini with RAG.

evidence.title: Improving Accuracy and Source Transparency in Responses to Soft Tissue Sarcoma Queries Using GPT-4o Enhanced with German Evidence-Based Guidelines
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy, comprehensiveness, safety and error rate of GPT-4o with vs without RAG on guidelines
evidence.effect: GPT-4o with RAG outperformed without RAG across all areas (p < 0.05); error rate fell from 40% to 10%.
evidence.quote: GPT-4o without RAG had a 40% error rate, which was reduced to 10% by the RAG approach.

evidence.title: Transforming the Landscape of Clinical Information Retrieval Using Generative Artificial Intelligence: An Application in Machine Fault Analysis
evidence.outcome: Response quality (hallucination, relevancy, correctness, completeness) with increasing source document context
evidence.effect: Responses improved with increasing source data context and more specific prompt construction, as rated by two board-certified medical physicists. No numbers reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Results indicated that responses improved with increasing source data context and more specific prompt construction.

evidence.title: Thyro-GenAI: A Chatbot Using Retrieval-Augmented Generative Models for Personalized Thyroid Disease Management

evidence.title: Detecting emergencies in patient portal messages using large language models and knowledge graph-based retrieval-augmented generation

evidence.title: Precision Oncology in Non-small Cell Lung Cancer: A Comparative Study of Contextualized ChatGPT Models

evidence.title: The Effectiveness of a Custom AI Chatbot for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Health Literacy: Development and Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: Appropriateness of RAG chatbot responses grounded in reference documents versus general knowledge

evidence.title: Comparison of artificial intelligence-generated and physician-generated patient education materials on early diabetic kidney disease

evidence.effect: No difference for ERNIE Bot 4.0; GPT-4o completeness differed (p=0.0156); ChatGLM4 did better without guidelines in completeness (p=0.0213) and safety (p=0.0300).
evidence.quote: Interestingly, in our study, LLMs performed worse with guidelines than without guidelines.

evidence.title: Performance evaluation of large language models in pediatric nephrology clinical decision support: a comprehensive assessment

evidence.quote: General-purpose LLMs rarely produced relevant, evidence-based answers (2-10% of questions).

evidence.title: Performance of ChatGPT-4o and Four Open-Source Large Language Models in Generating Diagnoses Based on China's Rare Disease Catalog: Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of qwen2.5:7b with versus without retrieval-augmented generation

evidence.title: Multimodal reasoning agent for enhanced ophthalmic decision-making: a preliminary real-world clinical validation

evidence.title: Evaluating a Chatbot as a Companion for Patients With Breast Cancer: Collaborative Pilot Study
evidence.outcome: Correctness, completeness, and harm of RAG-grounded GPT-4 answers rated against guidelines

evidence.title: Augmenting Large Language Models With National Comprehensive Cancer Network Guidelines for Improved and Standardized Adjuvant Therapy Recommendations in Postoperative Breast Cancer Cases

evidence.title: Performance of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Large Language Models in Guideline-Concordant Prostate-Specific Antigen Testing: Comparative Study With Junior Clinicians

evidence.title: Performance of large language models in interventional cardiology: the ILLUMINATE blinded model-comparison study

evidence.effect: PULSE improved clinical accuracy, content integrity, utility, and safety (P < 0.05) across all tested models versus base LLMs.
evidence.quote: The results demonstrated that PULSE improved clinical accuracy, content integrity, utility, and safety (P < 0.05) across all tested models.

evidence.title: Optimizing GPT-5 for Operation-Procedure-Code-Extraction from Operative Reports in Meningioma Surgery: Feasibility and Comparison of Context-Enhancements
evidence.outcome: Correct OPS coding and hallucination counts with versus without retrieved/curated context files
evidence.effect: Correct coding rose from 44% (no context) to 79% (rules), 70% (examples), 86% (combined); hallucinations fell from 105 to 8, 2, and 6 respectively (p<0.001).
evidence.quote: Our data strongly support the thesis that contextualization significantly reduces hallucinations and thus leads to a great increase in quality.

evidence.title: End-to-End Pipeline Integrating Local Small Language Models and Machine Learning for Data Extraction and Stroke Outcome Prediction in Emergency Department
evidence.outcome: Extraction accuracy before and after RAG-based verification against source text
evidence.effect: Accuracy increased from 74.8% (rule-based) to 86.0% after RAG validation; grounding accuracy 91.5%; improvement significant (P<0.001).
evidence.quote: After RAG-based contextual validation, accuracy increased further to 86.0% (95% CI, 83.6% to 88.4%), with F1 score and variable-level F1 both 0.813 (95% CI, 0.791 to 0.835).

evidence.title: Multispecialty Dental EMRs from Chairside Audio: An Exploratory Study
evidence.outcome: Output variability and medical accuracy with vs without evidence capture and consensus voting modules
evidence.effect: System 2 reduced standard deviation by 33.8% (periodontics), 55.9% (orthodontics), and 42.6% (prosthodontics), with improved medical accuracy and consistency; largest gains in complex prosthodontic cases.
evidence.quote: System 2 improved robustness with standard deviation reductions of 33.8% (periodontics), 55.9% (orthodontics), and 42.6% (prosthodontics), with the largest gains in complex prosthodontic cases.

evidence.title: Comparative Assessment of Performance of Domain-Specific and Primed Versus Non-Primed Artificial Intelligence Chatbots for Clinical Decision-Making in Injuries to the Primary Dentition: An Exploratory Pilot Study
evidence.venue: Dental traumatology : official publication of International Association for Dental Traumatology
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of general-purpose chatbot responses with vs without guideline priming versus IADT guidelines
evidence.effect: Priming significantly improved general-purpose chatbots; ChatGPT and Perplexity showed marked gains in follow-up interval accuracy and radiographic recommendations.
evidence.quote: Priming significantly improved the performance of general-purpose chatbots, with ChatGPT and Perplexity demonstrating marked gains in follow-up interval accuracy and radiographic recommendations.

evidence.title: A Multiagent Large Language Model Framework for Emergency Treatment Recommendation in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Development and Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Hallucination and omission rates and safety scores with guideline-based multiagent framework
evidence.effect: Mean clinical safety score rose from 3.70 to 4.01; hallucination rate fell from 33.6% to 20.6% and omission rate from 38.5% to 24.5%.
evidence.quote: Across evaluated models, the multiagent framework increased the mean clinical safety score from 3.70 to 4.01 and reduced mean hallucination and omission rates from 33.6% to 20.6% and from 38.5% to 24.5%, respectively.
evidence.sample_unit: cases (1055 group A, 721 group B, 144 group C, 161 group D)

evidence.title: Finite State Machine-Guided Retrieval-Augmented Generation Improves Expert-Rated Acceptability of a Peripherally Inserted Central Catheter Self-Management Chatbot: Single-Center Content Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Expert preference between fine-tuned model with and without RAG grounding
evidence.effect: Model 2 (FT+RAG) did not differ from model 1 (FT only) in expert preference after Bonferroni correction; adding FSM (model 3) was preferred in 34/43 (79.1%) scenarios.
evidence.quote: Pairwise McNemar tests showed model 3 was preferred significantly more often than model 1 and model 2 (both P<.001), while model 1 versus model 2 did not differ after Bonferroni correction.

evidence.title: Development of a Guideline-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation Chatbot Referencing Web-Based Cancer Clinical Practice Guidelines
evidence.outcome: Hallucinations in RAG chatbot answers grounded in guideline content, manual review of in-scope questions
evidence.effect: No hallucinations were identified during manual review under the defined test conditions for in-scope questions.
evidence.quote: For in-scope questions, the chatbot generated responses by summarizing guideline content, and no hallucinations were identified during manual review under the defined test conditions.

evidence.title: Improving Pelvic Floor Disorder Education: A Second Pilot of a Retrieval-Augmented AI Chatbot Model
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated response quality (QAMAI) and usability (SUS) of a chatbot grounded in AUGS materials
evidence.effect: Median QAMAI score 28 (IQR 24-29.8); mean SUS 81.8 ± 11.2; no comparator arm in this pilot; citation consistency and clinical depth noted as needing improvement.
evidence.quote: A retrieval-augmented ChatGPT model trained on AUGS materials generated high-quality responses with excellent usability.

evidence.title: Improvement of Clinical Practice Guideline Appraisal by Human Experts and AI Agents by Using Structured Guidance: Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, and Validation Study
evidence.outcome: AI agent-human agreement on AGREE II with vs without workbook grounding via retrieval
evidence.effect: Workbook raised DeepSeek-R1 ICC from 0.613 to 0.709 and o1-mini from 0.629 to 0.687; agreement still below human-human 0.752.
evidence.quote: Using the arithmetic mean across expert 1 and expert 2 consistently for both models, the modified ICC for DeepSeek-R1 rose from 0.613 to 0.709, while o1-mini increased from 0.629 to 0.687.

evidence.title: TCM-CoT-RAG: a chain-of-thought enhanced retrieval-augmented generation system for clinical decision support in Traditional Chinese Medicine rheumatology
evidence.outcome: Entity and Formula F1 and BERTScore for RAG-grounded CoT versus baseline LLM on TCM rheumatology cases
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-V3 with full-chain CoT-RAG reached Entity F1 44.89% (+16.45% over baseline), Formula F1 32.13% (+8.74%), and BERTScore 0.81.
evidence.quote: DeepSeek-V3 with full-chain CoT-RAG achieved Entity F1 of 44.89% (+16.45% over baseline) and Formula F1 of 32.13% (+8.74% over baseline), with BERTScore of 0.81 indicating strong semantic alignment with expert reasoning.
evidence.sample_unit: expert-curated clinical cases held out for evaluation (50 also blindly reviewed by experts)

evidence.title: Evaluating large language model clinical reasoning in glaucoma using retrieval-augmented generation
evidence.venue: Advances in ophthalmology practice and research
evidence.outcome: Guideline quality of glaucoma management responses with vs without RAG grounding, rated by masked specialists
evidence.effect: Human-rated composite RAG advantage: GPT 0.119 (95% CI 0.068-0.173), Gemini 0.095 (0.030-0.161), Grok 0.110 (0.033-0.194); pooled 0.114 excluding Gemini.
evidence.quote: RAG maintained a significant composite advantage over matched non-RAG models for GPT (mean difference=0.119, 95% CI: 0.068–0.173, Wilcoxon P =0.0002), Gemini (mean difference=0.095, 95% CI: 0.030–0.161, P =0.0098), and Grok (mean difference=0.110, 95% CI: 0.033–0.194, P =0.0155).

evidence.title: Evaluation of a cornea-specialized large language model for diagnostic and management accuracy in complex corneal cases
evidence.outcome: Clinician diagnostic accuracy with RAG-grounded specialized LLM versus general GPT-4o and unaided
evidence.effect: Diagnostic accuracy unaided 48.7%, 20.5%, 38.5%; general GPT-4o 69.2%, 46.2%, 59.0%; RAG-specialized 71.8%, 48.7%, 74.4%, improved over unaided for all clinicians (p<0.01).
evidence.quote: The cornea-specialized GPT-4o further improved accuracy to 71.8%, 48.7%, and 74.4%, with improvements over unaided performance for all clinicians (p<0.01).
evidence.sample_unit: cornea trainees (each reviewing 39 real-world corneal cases under three conditions)

evidence.title: Evaluating a Guideline-Integrated Clinical Interaction Framework Vs a Standard Large Language Model Interaction for Dietary Recommendations in Recurrent Urolithiasis: In Silico Study
evidence.outcome: Guideline adherence of guideline-integrated framework vs standard LLM on urolithiasis dietary advice
evidence.effect: Guideline adherence median 5.00 (IQR 5.00-5.00) vs 3.67 (IQR 3.08-4.00), P<.001 in structured inputs; retained in query-style inputs (5.00 vs 4.00, P<.001).
evidence.quote: StoneAgent also showed higher guideline adherence than the standard LLM in the structured-input experiment (median 5.00, IQR 5.00‐5.00 vs median 3.67, IQR 3.08‐4.00; P <.001).

evidence.title: [Can ChatGPT Responses Be Improved by Incorporating S3 Clinical Practice Guidelines?]
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy of ChatGPT answers with vs without guideline PDF provided
evidence.effect: Accuracy improved with guideline PDF (1.77 vs. 1.26; p = 0.003); conciseness also improved (1.96 vs. 1.50; p = 0.004).
evidence.quote: Providing the guideline as a PDF together with the respective question resulted in a significant improvement in accuracy (1.77 vs. 1.26; p = 0.003) and conciseness (1.96 vs. 1.50; p = 0.004).

evidence.title: Locally Deployed Large Language Models for AI-Assisted Outpatient Prescription Review: Crossover Study
evidence.outcome: LLM hallucination rate with vs without knowledge augmentation from package inserts
evidence.effect: Hallucination rate fell from 19.7% (42/213) to 4.7% (10/213), absolute reduction 15.0 percentage points (relative 76.2%; P<.001)
evidence.quote: Knowledge augmentation reduced the model hallucination rate from 19.7% (42/213 prescriptions) to 4.7% (10/213), an absolute reduction of 15.0 percentage points (relative reduction 76.2%; P<.001).

evidence.title: A medically grounded LLM agent-based tool to detect patient safety events in medical records
evidence.outcome: Accuracy detecting epinephrine adverse safety events versus baseline LLMs, using ontology and strict rules
evidence.effect: SAFE-AI reached 97.9% accuracy for epinephrine overdoses and 91.6% for delays in epinephrine administration, greatly outperforming baseline LLMs.
evidence.quote: We tested SAFE-AI against these labels, achieving similar performance to human experts in detecting epinephrine overdoses with 97.9% accuracy, and 91.6% accuracy in identifying delays in epinephrine administration, greatly outperforming baseline LLMs models.
evidence.sample_unit: EMS clinical charts (18,402 lines of clinical information)

evidence.title: Concordance between GPT-4 and a multidisciplinary tumor board in pancreatic cancer: A prospective pilot study
evidence.outcome: Concordance with MDT before vs after prompting GPT-4 with 41 curated abstracts
evidence.effect: Concordance unchanged at 73.3% (κ 0.64 to 0.61); 31 of 41 abstracts (75.4%) never cited; only 1 of 45 cases changed recommendation.
evidence.quote: Additional literature prompting did not result in any cases in which GPT-4’s recommendations became concordant with those of the MDT (33 cases, 73.3%, κ = 0.61, p < 0.0001, Fig. 1 ), indicating substantial agreement in both scenarios.

evidence.title: Improving Reliability and Explainability of Medical Question Answering Through Atomic Fact-Checking in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models: Creation and Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Whether post-hoc verification against guideline evidence improves factuality beyond RAG grounding
evidence.effect: Atomic fact-checking added to RAG improved answer quality; answers improved in 20%, 10%, 50% and 7.7% of cases versus worsened in 8%, 0%, 7.5% and 3%.
evidence.quote: However, since the proportion of answers that improved (20%, 10%, 50%, and 7.7%) was substantially higher, the overall effect of fact-checking clearly enhanced the answer quality.

evidence.title: TracSum: A New Benchmark for Aspect-Based Summarization with Sentence-Level Traceability in Medical Domain
evidence.outcome: Summary accuracy and completeness with vs without prior sentence-level evidence tracking
evidence.effect: Explicit sentence-level tracking before summarization enhanced generation accuracy; adding full context further improved completeness. No numbers reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: We also observe that explicitly performing sentence-level tracking prior to summarization enhances generation accuracy, while incorporating the full context further improves completeness.

evidence.title: End-to-End Agentic RAG System Training for Traceable Diagnostic Reasoning
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of RL-trained agentic RAG versus prompt-engineering and training-free RAG methods
evidence.effect: End-to-end RL agentic RAG consistently outperformed prompt-engineering and training-free RAG; average accuracy gain of 22.7% over the second-best model on ID and OOD benchmarks.
evidence.quote: Experiments show our end-to-end RL framework consistently outperforms prompt-engineering and training-free RAG methods.

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Evidence-Based Clinical Question Answering
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on previously incorrect items with and without retrieved abstracts in the prompt
evidence.effect: Gold-source abstract raised accuracy on previously incorrect items to 0.79; top 3 PubMed abstracts improved it to 0.23; random abstracts reduced it to 0.10 (within temperature variation).
evidence.quote: When we incorporate retrieval-augmented prompting, providing the gold-source abstract raises accuracy on previously incorrect items to 0.79; providing top 3 PubMed abstracts (ranked by semantic relevance) improves accuracy to 0.23, while random abstracts reduce accuracy (0.10, within temperature variation).

evidence.title: Adapting and Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models for Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Self-Management: A Divide and Conquer Framework
evidence.outcome: MLLM performance on the AIS knowledge assessment task with versus without retrieval augmented generation
evidence.effect: RAG substantially improved models' performance on the knowledge assessment task. No numeric effect sizes are given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Results showed varying effectiveness of visual prompting across different architectures, while RAG substantially improved models' performances on the knowledge assessment task.
evidence.sample_unit: anteroposterior X-rays with diagnostic texts (approximate database size)

evidence.title: Combating Biomedical Misinformation through Multi-modal Claim Detection and Evidence-based Verification
evidence.outcome: Hallucination mitigation and claim verification performance when LLM outputs are grounded in retrieved biomedical evidence
evidence.effect: Authors report CER, which grounds LLM reasoning in retrieved scientific evidence, mitigates hallucination risk and achieves state-of-the-art performance on HealthFC, BioASQ-7b, and SciFact; no numeric results in provided text.
evidence.quote: By integrating the text-generation capabilities of large language models with advanced retrieval techniques for high-quality biomedical scientific evidence, CER effectively mitigates the risk of hallucinations, ensuring that generated outputs are grounded in verifiable, evidence-based sources.
evidence.sample_unit: claims (benchmark datasets HealthFC, BioASQ-7b, SciFact; counts not reported in text)

evidence.title: An Automated Retrieval-Augmented Generation LLaMA-4 109B-based System for Evaluating Radiotherapy Treatment Plans
evidence.outcome: Agreement of LLM outputs with values computed by retrieval and constraint-checking modules
evidence.effect: RAG system achieved 100% agreement with standalone retrieval and constraint-checking values on percentile estimates and constraint identification; no comparison against a non-grounded LLM.
evidence.quote: When tested end-to-end, the RAG system achieved 100% agreement with the computed values by standalone retrieval and constraint-checking modules on both percentile estimates and constraint identification, confirming reliable execution of all retrieval, prediction and checking steps.

evidence.title: MedMMV: A Controllable Multimodal Multi-Agent Framework for Reliable and Verifiable Clinical Reasoning
evidence.outcome: Reasoning truthfulness and accuracy when grounding intermediate steps in a structured evidence graph with a hallucination detector
evidence.effect: Accuracy improved by up to 12.7% on six medical benchmarks; blind physician evaluations showed substantially increased reasoning truthfulness without loss of informational content.
evidence.quote: Blind physician evaluations confirm that MedMMV substantially increases reasoning truthfulness without sacrificing informational content.

evidence.title: Grounding Large Language Models in Clinical Evidence: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Querying UK NICE Clinical Guidelines
evidence.outcome: Faithfulness of answers to source text with versus without retrieval-augmented grounding in NICE guidelines
evidence.effect: RAG raised faithfulness by 64.7 percentage points to 99.5% for O4-Mini; Meditron3-8B without RAG scored 43%.
evidence.quote: Faithfulness, the measure of whether an answer is supported by the source text, was increased by 64.7 percentage points to 99.5% for the RAG-enhanced O4-Mini model and significantly outperformed the medical-focused Meditron3-8B LLM, which scored 43%.

evidence.title: YpathRAG:A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework and Benchmark for Pathology
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy on hard pathology questions with vs without retrieval-augmented grounding
evidence.effect: YpathRAG increased accuracies of both general and medical LLMs by 9.0% on average and up to 15.6% on the 300 hardest YpathQA-M questions.
evidence.quote: on YpathQA-M, a set of the 300 most challenging questions, it increases the accuracies of both general and medical LLMs by 9.0% on average and up to 15.6%.

evidence.title: Demo: Guide-RAG: Evidence-Driven Corpus Curation for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Long COVID
evidence.outcome: LLM-judged faithfulness, relevance, comprehensiveness across six RAG corpus configurations for Long COVID questions
evidence.effect: Corpus combining clinical guidelines with high-quality systematic reviews consistently outperformed narrow single-guideline corpora and large-scale literature databases; no numeric results are given in the text.
evidence.quote: Our RAG corpus configuration combining clinical guidelines with high-quality systematic reviews consistently outperformed both narrow single-guideline approaches and large-scale literature databases.

evidence.title: ECG-LLM -- training and evaluation of domain-specific large language models for electrocardiography
evidence.outcome: Human expert preference for RAG-grounded outputs versus finetuned models on complex queries
evidence.effect: Human expert evaluation favored Claude 3.7 and RAG approaches for complex queries; no numeric effect reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Human expert evaluation favored Claude 3.7 and RAG approaches for complex queries.

evidence.title: Investigating LLM Capabilities on Long Context Comprehension for Medical Question Answering
evidence.outcome: Effect of retrieval augmentation on long-context medical QA comprehension across single- and multi-document datasets
evidence.effect: RAG excels in challenging cases and has best settings differing between single- and multi-document QA datasets, but shows limitations in cases requiring temporal reasoning. No numbers reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Our quantitative analysis reveals challenging cases where RAG excels while still showing limitations in cases requiring temporal reasoning.

evidence.title: CARE-RAG - Clinical Assessment and Reasoning in RAG
evidence.outcome: LLM reasoning accuracy on Written Exposure Therapy questions when authoritative guideline passages are provided via RAG
evidence.effect: Errors persisted even when authoritative passages were provided; RAG can constrain outputs, but reasoning must be assessed as rigorously as retrieval. No numbers reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Our results highlight both the potential and the risks: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can constrain outputs, but safe deployment requires assessing reasoning as rigorously as retrieval.

evidence.title: Leveraging Evidence-Guided LLMs to Enhance Trustworthy Depression Diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and confidence score of DSM-5-grounded evidence-guided prompting versus direct and CoT prompting
evidence.effect: On OpenBioLLM, EGDR raised accuracy from 0.31 (Direct) to 0.76 and DCS from 0.50 to 0.67. On MedLlama, DCS rose from 0.58 (CoT) to 0.77. Overall gains were up to +45% accuracy and +36% DCS.
evidence.quote: For instance, on OpenBioLLM, EGDR improves accuracy from 0.31 (Direct) to 0.76 and increases DCS from 0.50 to 0.67.

evidence.title: Optimizing Medical Question-Answering Systems: A Comparative Study of Fine-Tuned and Zero-Shot Large Language Models with RAG Framework
evidence.outcome: Answer accuracy and unsupported content with versus without retrieval grounding on medical QA benchmarks
evidence.effect: Fine-tuned LLaMA 2 with RAG reached 71.8% accuracy on PubMedQA vs 55.4% zero-shot baseline; grounding reduced unsupported content by approximately 60%.
evidence.quote: We also detail the system design and fine-tuning methodology, demonstrating that grounding answers in retrieved evidence reduces unsupported content by approximately 60%.

evidence.title: Knowledge-Guided Large Language Model for Automatic Pediatric Dental Record Understanding and Safe Antibiotic Recommendation
evidence.outcome: Effect of knowledge graph and RAG grounding on record understanding, antibiotic recommendation accuracy, and safety
evidence.effect: KG-LLM vs Llama-2 baseline: F1 0.914 vs 0.867, Top-1 dose-drug-duration accuracy 0.782 vs 0.716, unsafe antibiotic suggestions reduced by 50%; ablation shows KG and RAG each contribute substantially.
evidence.quote: Ablation analyses indicate that the knowledge graph, RAG, and safety modules each contribute substantially to clinical reliability and interpretability.

evidence.title: Clinical Knowledge Graph Construction and Evaluation with Multi-LLMs via Retrieval-Augmented Generation
evidence.outcome: Precision, relevance, and ontology compliance of KGs built with schema-constrained RAG vs baseline methods
evidence.effect: Reported consistent gains in precision, relevance, and ontology compliance over baseline methods; no numbers given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Experimental results demonstrate consistent gains in precision, relevance, and ontology compliance over baseline methods.
evidence.sample_unit: oncology cohorts (PDAC and BRCA) of clinical narratives

evidence.title: Self-MedRAG: a Self-Reflective Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Reliable Medical Question Answering
evidence.outcome: Benchmark QA accuracy with and without self-reflective evidence-verification loop over retrieval-grounded generation
evidence.effect: Self-reflective loop raised MedQA accuracy from 80.00% to 83.33% and PubMedQA accuracy from 69.10% to 79.82%; hybrid retrieval outperformed single-retriever baselines.
evidence.quote: Furthermore, the inclusion of the self-reflective loop yielded substantial gains, increasing accuracy on MedQA from 80.00% to 83.33% and on PubMedQA from 69.10% to 79.82%.

evidence.title: Bridging the Knowledge-Action Gap by Evaluating LLMs in Dynamic Dental Clinical Scenarios
evidence.outcome: Effect of retrieval-augmented generation on hallucinations in static tasks and dynamic dental workflows
evidence.effect: RAG mitigates hallucinations in static tasks, but its efficacy in dynamic workflows is limited and heterogeneous, sometimes causing degradation.
evidence.quote: While RAG mitigates hallucinations in static tasks, its efficacy in dynamic workflows is limited and heterogeneous, sometimes causing degradation.

evidence.title: Domain-Specific Knowledge Graphs in RAG-Enhanced Healthcare LLMs
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLMs with knowledge-graph RAG versus No-RAG across graph sources, probes and temperatures
evidence.effect: Scope-matched retrieval (notably G2) gave the most consistent gains; indiscriminate graph unions often reduced accuracy; larger models matched or exceeded KG-RAG with No-RAG on Probe 1.
evidence.quote: Results show that scope alignment between probe and KG is decisive: precise, scope-matched retrieval (notably $\mathbb{G}_2$) yields the most consistent gains, whereas indiscriminate graph unions often introduce distractors that reduce accuracy.

evidence.title: MRAG: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Bio-medicine
evidence.outcome: LLM reliability with versus without retrieval augmentation on medical QA benchmark tasks
evidence.effect: RAG enhanced LLM reliability across MRAG tasks; performance varied with retrieval approach, model size, and prompting strategy; long-form responses became slightly less readable.
evidence.quote: RAG enhances LLM reliability across MRAG tasks.

evidence.title: A Multi-Agent Framework for Medical AI: Leveraging Fine-Tuned GPT, LLaMA, and DeepSeek R1 for Evidence-Based and Bias-Aware Clinical Query Processing
evidence.outcome: Model uncertainty (perplexity) with vs without PubMed evidence augmentation
evidence.effect: Evidence augmentation reduced uncertainty (perplexity 4.13) compared to base responses; full system 87% accuracy, relevance around 0.80.
evidence.quote: In evaluation, the full system achieves 87% accuracy with relevance around 0.80, and evidence augmentation reduces uncertainty (perplexity 4.13) compared to base responses, with mean end-to-end latency of 36.5 seconds under the reported configuration.

evidence.title: Evidence-Grounded Subspecialty Reasoning: Evaluating a Curated Clinical Intelligence Layer on the 2025 Endocrinology Board-Style Examination
evidence.outcome: Board-exam accuracy of curated-evidence-grounded system vs web-retrieval frontier LLMs
evidence.effect: Mirror 87.5% (105/120) vs GPT-5.2 74.6%, GPT-5 74.0%, Gemini-3-Pro 69.8%; human reference 62.3%.
evidence.quote: Curated evidence with explicit provenance can outperform unconstrained web retrieval for subspecialty clinical reasoning and supports auditability for clinical deployment.

evidence.title: An artificial intelligence framework for end-to-end rare disease phenotyping from clinical notes using large language models
evidence.outcome: Ablation of extraction, ontology standardization, and prioritization modules on phenotyping performance
evidence.effect: Performance improved with the addition of each module, including ontology-grounded standardization to HPO terms; end-to-end ontology-based similarity 0.70 vs 0.58 for PhenoBERT.
evidence.quote: Ablation analyses demonstrated performance improvements with the addition of each module in RARE-PHENIX (extraction, standardization, and prioritization), supporting the value of modeling the full clinical phenotyping workflow.

evidence.title: CXReasonAgent: Evidence-Grounded Diagnostic Reasoning Agent for Chest X-rays
evidence.outcome: Faithful grounding and verifiability of diagnostic responses, tool-grounded agent versus LVLMs on multi-turn benchmark
evidence.effect: CXReasonAgent, which uses clinically grounded diagnostic tools, produced faithfully grounded responses and more reliable, verifiable diagnostic reasoning than LVLMs; no numeric results in the provided text.
evidence.quote: and show that CXReasonAgent produces faithfully grounded responses, enabling more reliable and verifiable diagnostic reasoning than LVLMs.

evidence.title: MED-COPILOT: A Medical Assistant Powered by GraphRAG and Similar Patient Case Retrieval
evidence.outcome: Note completion fidelity and medical QA accuracy with guideline-grounded GraphRAG versus parametric LLM and standard RAG
evidence.effect: GraphRAG with similar-patient retrieval consistently outperformed parametric LLM baselines and standard RAG, improving generation fidelity and clinical reasoning accuracy (no numbers in abstract).
evidence.quote: We evaluate our framework on clinical note completion and medical question answering, and demonstrate that it consistently outperforms parametric LLM baselines and standard RAG, improving both generation fidelity and clinical reasoning accuracy.

evidence.title: PanCanBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Pancreatic Oncology
evidence.outcome: Rubric score with versus without web-search grounding
evidence.effect: Web search did not improve scores: Gemini-2.5 Pro 66.8% to 63.9%; GPT-5 73.8% to 72.8% when web search was enabled.
evidence.quote: The average score changed from 66.8% to 63.9% for Gemini-2.5 Pro and from 73.8% to 72.8% for GPT-5 when web search was enabled.
evidence.sample_unit: authentic patient questions (3,130 expert rubric criteria)

evidence.title: MedCalc-Bench Doesn't Measure What You Think: A Benchmark Audit and the Case for Open-Book Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on clinical calculator tasks with vs without calculator specification in prompt
evidence.effect: Providing the calculator specification at inference (open-book) raised accuracy from ~52% to 81-85% on GLM-4.6V and GLM-4.7, without fine-tuning.
evidence.quote: Second, we show that a simple intervention-providing the model with the calculator specification at inference time ("open-book" prompting)-raises accuracy from ~52% to 81-85% on GLM-4.6V and GLM-4.7, surpassing all published results including RL-trained systems, without any fine-tuning.
