evidence.title: From Conflict to Consensus: Boosting Medical Reasoning via Multi-Round Agentic RAG
evidence.outcome: Medical Q&A accuracy of retrieval-grounded multi-round agentic RAG versus backbone and RAG baselines
evidence.effect: MA-RAG consistently surpassed inference-time scaling and RAG baselines across 7 medical Q&A benchmarks, with +6.8 points average accuracy over the backbone model.
evidence.quote: Extensive evaluations across 7 medical Q&A benchmarks show that MA-RAG consistently surpasses competitive inference-time scaling and RAG baselines, delivering substantial +6.8 points on average accuracy over the backbone model.

evidence.title: Agentic retrieval-augmented reasoning reshapes collective reliability under model variability in radiology question answering
evidence.outcome: Cross-model robustness of correctness and consensus with vs without evidence-grounded agentic retrieval
evidence.effect: Agentic retrieval reduced inter-model decision dispersion (median entropy 0.48 vs. 0.13) and increased robustness of correctness across models (mean 0.74 vs. 0.81); majority consensus increased (P<0.001).
evidence.quote: Agentic inference reduced inter-model decision dispersion (median entropy 0.48 vs. 0.13) and increased robustness of correctness across models (mean 0.74 vs. 0.81).

evidence.title: CORE-Acu: Structured Reasoning Traces and Knowledge Graph Safety Verification for Acupuncture Clinical Decision Support
evidence.outcome: Safety violation rate with knowledge-graph verification versus GPT-4o under identical rules
evidence.effect: CORE-Acu achieved 0/1,000 observed safety violations (95% CI: 0--0.37%), whereas GPT-4o exhibited an 8.5% violation rate under identical rules.
evidence.quote: Crucially, CORE-Acu achieved 0/1,000 observed safety violations (95\% CI: 0--0.37\%), whereas GPT-4o exhibited an 8.5\% violation rate under identical rules.

evidence.title: PREBA: Surgical Duration Prediction via PCA-Weighted Retrieval-Augmented LLMs and Bayesian Averaging Aggregation
evidence.outcome: Surgical duration prediction error (MAE, R^2) with retrieval-grounded prompts versus zero-shot LLM inference
evidence.effect: Reduced MAE by up to 40% and raised R^2 from -0.13 to 0.62 over zero-shot inference; accuracy competitive with supervised ML methods.
evidence.quote: PREBA significantly improves performance-for instance, reducing MAE by up to 40% and raising R^2 from -0.13 to 0.62 over zero-shot inference-and it achieves accuracy competitive with supervised ML methods, demonstrating strong effectiveness and generalization.

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Gait Classification Using Text-Encoded Kinematic Waveforms
evidence.outcome: LLM gait classification with vs without explicit reference gait statistics (grounding)
evidence.effect: Performance was highly dependent on explicit reference information; GPT-5 with reference grounding achieved multiclass MCC 0.70 and binary MCC 0.68.
evidence.quote: Performance of the LLM was highly dependent on explicit reference information and self-rated confidence; when restricted to high-confidence predictions, multiclass MCC increased to 0.83 on the filtered subset.

evidence.title: CURE: A Multimodal Benchmark for Clinical Understanding and Retrieval Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Differential diagnosis accuracy with physician reference evidence versus independent retrieval
evidence.effect: Up to 73.4% accuracy on differential diagnosis with physician reference evidence; as low as 25.4% when models relied on independent retrieval.
evidence.quote: Evaluations reveal a stark dichotomy: while advanced models demonstrate clinical reasoning proficiency when supplied with physician reference evidence (achieving up to $73.4\%$ accuracy on differential diagnosis), their performance substantially declines (as low as $25.4\%$) when reliant on independent retrieval mechanisms.

evidence.title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Extract and Translate Medical Information in Doctors' Notes for Health Records and Diagnostic Billing Codes
evidence.outcome: ICD-10-CM code accuracy with retrieval-augmented generation versus zero-shot and few-shot prompting
evidence.effect: RAG enabled limited discovery of unseen codes, but it frequently saturated context windows, reducing overall accuracy.
evidence.quote: While RAG enabled limited discovery of unseen codes, it frequently saturated context windows, reducing overall accuracy.

evidence.title: Knowledge-Guided Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Zero-Shot Psychiatric Data: Privacy Preserving Synthetic Data Generation
evidence.outcome: Fidelity of synthetic psychiatric data with vs without clinical knowledge retrieval
evidence.effect: Ablation showed clinical retrieval reliably improved univariate and pairwise fidelity over a no-retrieval LLM.
evidence.quote: An ablation study shows that clinical retrieval reliably improves univariate and pairwise fidelity over a no-retrieval LLM.

evidence.title: PubMed Reasoner: Dynamic Reasoning-based Retrieval for Evidence-Grounded Biomedical Question Answering
evidence.outcome: Biomedical QA accuracy and judged evidence grounding of retrieval-grounded answers with citations
evidence.effect: 78.32% accuracy on PubMedQA with GPT-4o, slightly above human experts; consistent gains on MMLU Clinical Knowledge; LLM judges preferred responses for evidence grounding.
evidence.quote: PubMed Reasoner with a GPT-4o backbone achieves 78.32% accuracy on PubMedQA, slightly surpassing human experts, and showing consistent gains on MMLU Clinical Knowledge.

evidence.title: A Systematic Study of Retrieval Pipeline Design for Retrieval-Augmented Medical Question Answering
evidence.outcome: Zero-shot medical QA accuracy with versus without retrieval augmentation on MedQA USMLE
evidence.effect: Retrieval augmentation significantly improved zero-shot accuracy; best configuration (dense retrieval with query reformulation and reranking) reached 60.49% accuracy.
evidence.quote: Results show that retrieval augmentation significantly improves zero-shot medical question answering performance.

evidence.title: Facet-Level Tracing of Evidence Uncertainty and Hallucination in RAG
evidence.outcome: Hallucination under Strict RAG, Soft RAG, and LLM-only modes in medical QA and HotpotQA
evidence.effect: Hallucinated answers remain common even when relevant documents are retrieved. Errors are driven less by retrieval accuracy and more by how retrieved evidence is integrated during generation. No numbers are reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Our results demonstrate that hallucinations in RAG systems are driven less by retrieval accuracy and more by how retrieved evidence is integrated during generation, with facet-level analysis exposing systematic evidence override and misalignment patterns that remain hidden under answer-level evaluation.

evidence.title: Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models for Evidence-Informed Guidance on Cannabidiol Use in Older Adults
evidence.outcome: Caution and guideline alignment of cannabidiol advice from retrieval-augmented versus standalone LLMs, judged by automated evaluation
evidence.effect: Across three automated evaluation strategies, retrieval-augmented models produced more cautious and guideline-aligned recommendations than standalone models; the ensemble retrieval approach performed best.
evidence.quote: Across three automated evaluation strategies, retrieval-augmented models consistently produced more cautious and guideline-aligned recommendations than standalone models, with the ensemble approach performing best.

evidence.title: Effects of Cross-lingual Evidence in Multilingual Medical Question Answering
evidence.outcome: Medical QA accuracy with versus without retrieved or curated external evidence across languages and model sizes
evidence.effect: External knowledge did not systematically improve performance. English web retrieval helped most for high-resource languages. English plus target-language retrieval helped low-resource languages. PubMed lacked multilingual coverage.
evidence.quote: These findings challenge the assumption that external knowledge systematically improves performance and reveal that effective strategies depend on both the source of language resources and on model scale.

evidence.title: Domain Fine-Tuning vs. Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medical Multiple-Choice Question Answering: A Controlled Comparison at the 4B-Parameter Scale
evidence.outcome: MedQA-USMLE majority-vote accuracy with versus without retrieved passages inserted into the prompt
evidence.effect: RAG over MedMCQA explanations gave no statistically significant gain in either model; in MedGemma the point estimate was -1.9 pp (p = 0.16).
evidence.quote: RAG over MedMCQA explanations does not produce a statistically significant gain in either model, and in the domain-tuned model the point estimate is slightly negative (-1.9 pp, p = 0.16).

evidence.title: Quantum Knowledge Graph: Modeling Context-Dependent Triplet Validity
evidence.outcome: Medical QA accuracy with vs without knowledge-graph-backed validation of LLM reasoner outputs
evidence.effect: With Haiku-4.5, KG validation gave +0.61 pp over no validator; QKG with context matching gave +1.40 pp over no validator and +0.79 pp over KG without context matching (all p<0.05). With Qwen-3.6-Plus, QKG gain over no validator was +5.96 pp.
evidence.quote: With Haiku-4.5 as both the Reasoner and the Validator, KG-backed validation significantly improves over a no-validator baseline ($+0.61$ pp), and QKG with context matching yields the largest gain, outperforming both KG validation without context matching ($+0.79$ pp) and the no-validator baseline ($+1.40$ pp; paired McNemar, all $p<0.05$).

evidence.title: Safety and accuracy follow different scaling laws in clinical large language models
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and safety errors with clean clinician-defined evidence versus closed-book prompting across 34 LLMs
evidence.effect: Mean accuracy rose from 73.5% to 94.1%; high-risk error fell from 12.0% to 2.6%; contradiction from 12.7% to 2.3%; dangerous overconfidence from 8.0% to 1.6%.
evidence.quote: Clean evidence produced the strongest improvement, increasing mean accuracy from 73.5% to 94.1%, while reducing high-risk error from 12.0% to 2.6%, contradiction from 12.7% to 2.3%, and dangerous overconfidence from 8.0% to 1.6%.

evidence.title: Safety and accuracy follow different scaling laws in clinical large language models
evidence.outcome: Safety of standard and agentic RAG retrieval grounding versus clean evidence
evidence.effect: Standard and agentic RAG did not reproduce clean-evidence safety; agentic RAG improved accuracy and reduced contradiction, but high-risk error and dangerous overconfidence remained elevated.
evidence.quote: Standard RAG and agentic RAG did not reproduce this safety profile: agentic RAG improved accuracy over standard RAG and reduced contradiction, but high-risk error and dangerous overconfidence remained elevated.

evidence.title: Research on Security Enhancement Methods for Adversarial Robust Large Language Model Intelligent Agents for Medical Decision-Making Tasks
evidence.outcome: Effect of removing evidence retrieval module on accuracy and attack success rate
evidence.effect: Removing evidence retrieval reduced accuracy by 9.1% and increased attack success rate by 11.1% in ablation.
evidence.quote: Ablation experiments quantify each module's contribution: removing risk perception, evidence retrieval, consistency verification, and confidence reweighting reduces accuracy by 6.7%, 9.1%, 7.6%, and 4.4%, respectively, and increases attack success rate by 13.8%, 11.1%, 8.6%, and 6.9%.

evidence.title: EpiGraph: Building Generalists for Evidence-Intensive Epilepsy Reasoning in the Wild
evidence.outcome: LLM performance on five epilepsy tasks with vs without Graph-RAG grounding in the knowledge graph
evidence.effect: Graph-RAG consistently improved performance across all tasks for six LLMs, with the largest gains in pharmacogenomic reasoning (+30-41%).
evidence.quote: Results show that integrating \textsc{EpiGraph} consistently improves performance across all tasks, with the largest gains observed in pharmacogenomic reasoning (+30--41\%).

evidence.title: MedMeta: A Benchmark for LLMs in Synthesizing Meta-Analysis Conclusion from Medical Studies
evidence.outcome: Meta-analysis conclusion quality with ground-truth retrieved abstracts (Golden-RAG) versus parametric-only generation
evidence.effect: Golden-RAG consistently and significantly outperformed Parametric-only across models; domain-specific fine-tuning benefits were marginal and neutralized when external material was provided. Best scores were only ~2.7/5.0.
evidence.quote: Our findings underscore the critical importance of information grounding: the Golden-RAG workflow consistently and significantly outperforms the Parametric-only approach across models.

evidence.title: ClinicalBench: Stress-Testing Assertion-Aware Retrieval for Cross-Admission Clinical QA on MIMIC-IV
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of assertion-aware knowledge-graph retrieval grounding versus LLM-alone baseline on clinical QA
evidence.effect: Author-blind primary endpoint +22.0 percentage points (95% Newcombe CI +5.1 to +31.5, p=0.0192); intent-aware KG-RAG over dense-RAG baseline +8.84 pp (p=1.79e-3).
evidence.quote: The author-blind primary endpoint, leave-author-out paired exact McNemar on 50 unanimous-strict items rated by two external physicians, yields +22.0 percentage points (95 percent Newcombe CI [+5.1, +31.5], p=0.0192).

evidence.title: Large Language Models Lack Temporal Awareness of Medical Knowledge
evidence.outcome: Effect of agentic search tool integration on temporal awareness accuracy
evidence.effect: Agentic search did not easily solve the temporal awareness problem; accuracy changes ranged from -3.15% to 14.14%.
evidence.quote: We also show that the temporal awareness problem is a challenge that cannot be easily solved when integrated with agentic search tools (-3.15%-14.14%).

evidence.title: ProtoMedAgent: Multimodal Clinical Interpretability via Privacy-Aware Agentic Workflows
evidence.outcome: Comparison Set Faithfulness of generated reports, constrained framework versus standard RAG
evidence.effect: ProtoMedAgent achieved 91.2% Comparison Set Faithfulness versus 46.2% for standard RAG.
evidence.quote: Evaluated on a 4,160-patient clinical cohort, ProtoMedAgent achieves 91.2% Comparison Set Faithfulness where it fundamentally outperforms standard RAG (46.2%).

evidence.title: When Cases Get Rare: A Retrieval Benchmark for Off-Guideline Clinical Question Answering
evidence.outcome: Correct answer rate on off-guideline clinical questions with vs without retrieved medical articles
evidence.effect: Best baseline GPT-5.2 answered 56% correctly and specialized models reached 42%; retrieval augmentation improved performance to up to 82% (GPT-5.2).
evidence.quote: Augmenting models with retrieved medical articles improves this performance to up to 82% (using GPT-5.2) highlighting the importance of evidence-grounding for real-world medical reasoning tasks.

evidence.title: IyàwóBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Model Clinical Triage Accuracy on Undifferentiated Febrile Illness in Nigerian Primary Health Settings
evidence.outcome: Triage accuracy of guideline-embedded systems versus general-purpose models
evidence.effect: Clinically engineered systems with embedded WHO guidelines outperformed general-purpose models by up to 28.5 percentage points in triage accuracy.
evidence.quote: Clinically engineered systems with embedded WHO guidelines outperform general-purpose models by up to 28.5 percentage points.

evidence.title: DrugClaw and DrugAudit: A Primary-Source-Grounded Agent and Authority-Aware Benchmark for Drug-Information Question Answering
evidence.outcome: Primary-source rate and citation faithfulness of a retrieval-grounded drug QA agent versus next-best baselines
evidence.effect: DrugClaw primary-source rate 0.918 (+10.1 pp over next-best); faithfulness 0.887 (+5.9 pp); MedQA 0.920; PubMedQA 0.693.
evidence.quote: Across DrugAudit plus drug-related subsets of MedQA (751) and PubMedQA (512), DrugClaw is top-1 on every column of the headline table: composite Evidence Index under both judges, judge-mediated answer correctness, primary-source rate (0.918, +10.1 pp over next-best), faithfulness (0.887, +5.9 pp), MedQA (0.920), and PubMedQA (0.693).

evidence.title: Trust but Verify: Mitigating Medical Hallucinations via Post-Hoc Adversarial Auditing and Multi-Agent Feedback Loops
evidence.outcome: Hallucination Error Rate with vs without agentic pipeline using real-time regulatory data
evidence.effect: The agentic architecture reduced HER by approximately 53% across models compared with vanilla conditions. Pointwise scores shifted from -0.25 toward 0.0.
evidence.quote: Our proposed agentic architecture reduced HER by approximately 53% across models.

evidence.title: RASC+: Retrieval-Constrained LLM Adjudication for Clinical Value Set Authoring
evidence.outcome: Value set completion macro F1 with retrieval-constrained LLM adjudication versus SAPBert selector over same pool
evidence.effect: Full-test macro F1 rose from 0.287 (SAPBert) to 0.549 (GPT-5); held-out-publisher macro F1 rose from 0.233 to 0.533, with all codes drawn from an auditable candidate pool.
evidence.quote: These results show that retrieval-constrained LLM adjudication can substantially improve value set completion while preserving the safety constraint that all returned codes must come from an auditable candidate pool.

evidence.title: T2D-Bench: Evidence-Gated Evaluation of LLM Outputs for Type 2 Diabetes Using a Multi-Layer Clinical-Lifestyle Knowledge Graph
evidence.outcome: Compliance with graph-checkable evidence requirements after constrained revision of LLM outputs
evidence.effect: Baseline outputs failed evidence-path checks in 35% (GPT-4o-mini) and 33% (GPT-4o) of 100 vignettes; constrained revision brought outputs into verifier-level compliance.
evidence.quote: The evidence gate detects unsupported omissions and uses constrained revision to bring outputs into verifier-level compliance with benchmark-defined evidence requirements.

evidence.title: MAM-AI: An On-Device Medical Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Nurses and Midwives in Zanzibar
evidence.outcome: Effect of retrieved guideline context on small generator answer quality and faithfulness
evidence.effect: Adding retrieved context did not improve the 4B generator's answers. Where the corpus held the right passage, answers were specific and actionable; otherwise they were vague. The chosen generator was about twice as faithful to its sources.
evidence.quote: The small generator is what remains in doubt: adding retrieved context does not improve its answers, and at 4B it cannot be both helpful and safe at once -- of two same-size candidates, the more helpful one commits genuine dangerous errors, so we deploy the other, which is about twice as faithful to its sources (as faithful as a frontier model), and recover its helpfulness with a redesigned prompt that cuts deflection from 33% to 3%.

evidence.title: Healthier LLMs: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Public Health Question Answering
evidence.outcome: Multiple-choice accuracy of LLMs with versus without retrieved context from UK public health guidance
evidence.effect: Retrieved context substantially increased multiple-choice accuracy across diverse LLMs; smaller open-weight models with retrieval matched or outperformed larger models without retrieval. Gains were driven by retrieval quality and context selection.
evidence.quote: Providing retrieved context substantially increases multiple-choice accuracy across a diverse set of LLMs, enabling smaller open-weight models to match or outperform larger models used without retrieval, with gains primarily driven by retrieval quality and careful context selection.

evidence.title: Faithful by Design: Evaluating and Improving LLM-Generated Clinical Trial Summaries for Multi-Stakeholder Audiences
evidence.outcome: NLI-based faithfulness of trial summaries with vs without knowledge-graph-augmented retrieval
evidence.effect: Knowledge-graph-augmented retrieval produced statistically significant improvements in NLI faithfulness scores (entailment +0.0125, faithfulness +0.0130, p < 0.0001) versus baseline; effects were small and model-dependent.
evidence.quote: A knowledge-graph-augmented retrieval system was developed and evaluated against the baseline, producing statistically significant improvements in NLI-based faithfulness scores (entailment +0.0125, faithfulness +0.0130, p < 0.0001).
evidence.sample_unit: generated summaries (200 trials x 3 audiences x 3 models)

evidence.title: MamaBench: Benchmarking LLM Robustness in Maternal and Child Health Diagnosis through Counterfactual Clinical Perturbation
evidence.outcome: Bias Trap Rate and base accuracy with retrieval-grounded method (EA-RAG) on Claude Sonnet 4.6
evidence.effect: EA-RAG achieved 20.3% BTR and 65.0% robust accuracy, a 5.5 percentage point BTR reduction without degrading base accuracy.
evidence.quote: EA-RAG achieves 20.3% BTR and 65.0% robust accuracy on Claude Sonnet 4.6, a 5.5 percentage point BTR reduction without degrading base accuracy.

evidence.title: A Knowledge-Injection Framework for Zero-Shot Adaptation of LLMs to Delirium Prediction
evidence.outcome: Delirium prediction AUROC with vs without injected clinical knowledge report, and with random control reports
evidence.effect: Clinically meaningful knowledge report improved AUROC by 8.57 points (8B) and 1.99 points (70B); random control reports did not improve and often degraded performance.
evidence.quote: Adding a clinically meaningful external knowledge report improves AUROC by 8.57 percentage points for the 8B model and 1.99 percentage points for the 70B model compared to no external knowledge.

evidence.title: Enhancing Explainable Cardiac Diagnosis with Guide-Grounded Multimodal LLMs
evidence.outcome: Semantic similarity (BERTScore) of generated ECG impressions to reference reports, with vs without guide grounding
evidence.effect: Average BERTScore rose from 0.818 to 0.953 versus the CNN+Grad-CAM+MLLM baseline without the guide, while classification performance stayed competitive.
evidence.quote: In particular, our method increases the average BERTScore of generated impressions from 0.818 to 0.953 relative to a strong CNN+Grad-CAM+MLLM baseline, indicat- ing closer alignment with reference reports.

evidence.title: Why LLMs Give In: Conversational Factors and Reasoning Behind Medical Sycophancy
evidence.outcome: Sycophancy rate with versus without grounding in retrieved or curated context
evidence.effect: Grounding reduced sycophancy but did not eliminate it (no numbers in abstract).
evidence.quote: Grounding helps, but does not eliminate the behavior.

evidence.title: Coupled Graph--Policy Distillation for Personalized Medication Safety in Older Adults with Multimorbidity
evidence.outcome: Strict Success Rate and safety reasoning of guideline-graph-grounded agent versus baseline LLMs
evidence.effect: Exceeds strongest proprietary LLM baseline by 53.73 points in Strict Success Rate and 14.63 points in OSRS, with no unsafe recommendations under the automated evaluator.
evidence.quote: On the European non-interactive multimorbidity benchmark, it exceeds the strongest proprietary LLM baseline by 53.73 points in Strict Success Rate and 14.63 points in overall safety reasoning score (OSRS), with no unsafe recommendations under the automated evaluator.

evidence.title: A corpus-specific clinical RAG system matches or outperforms newer frontier LLMs on HealthBench
evidence.outcome: HealthBench rubric score of corpus-grounded RAG system versus frontier LLMs without that corpus
evidence.effect: VITA ranked first (51.9% vs GPT-5.4 46.1%) on 4,023 questions. On the 500-question subset with newer models and a neutral judge, VITA and GPT-5.5 were statistically indistinguishable; VITA's communication scores were lower.
evidence.quote: Here the gap narrowed to parity: VITA and GPT-5.5 were statistically indistinguishable on mean per-question score, while VITA led on points-weighted score and won the most questions.

evidence.title: Framework for Grounding Healthcare LLMs in a Causal Knowledge Graph: A Cardiovascular Example Pilot
evidence.outcome: Effect of knowledge-graph and causal-graph grounding on LLM causal, evidence, unsupported-claim, and intervention accuracy metrics
evidence.effect: Integrated grounding (C4) had the best causal edge F1 (0.838), adverse-effect F1 (0.833), evidence accuracy (0.738) and unsupported claim rate (0.114); ungrounded C1 had the highest raw intervention accuracy (0.948).
evidence.quote: The metric panel discriminates conditions along interpretable, non-redundant axes: C4 obtains the strongest causal edge F1 (0.838), adverse-effect F1 (0.833), evidence accuracy (0.738), and unsupported claim rate (0.114), while C1 obtains the highest raw intervention accuracy (0.948) with no measurable causal or evidential grounding.

evidence.title: Dissecting Neuro-Symbolic Quality Assurance for Synthetic Oncology Data Generation
evidence.outcome: Effect of retrieval augmentation on gate compliance across generators
evidence.effect: Retrieval improves gate compliance for one generator by 12.5 percentage points, has no measurable effect for a second, and collapses output in a third.
evidence.quote: Retrieval augmentation is strongly model-dependent: it improves gate compliance for one generator by 12.5 percentage points, has no measurable effect for a second, and collapses output in a third.

evidence.title: TSWAP: A Multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Thai Wellness Advisor
evidence.outcome: Verifiable provider recommendations with vs without knowledge-base grounding
evidence.effect: Without the knowledge base, the model produced zero verifiable provider recommendations; forced-retrieval routing was necessary for reliable grounding.
evidence.quote: We further report two transferable deployment findings: English-calibrated 4-bit AWQ quantization corrupts Thai tone marks, and forced-retrieval routing is necessary for reliable grounding.

evidence.title: Standalone LLM and a Pre-specified Agentic Pipeline for Explaining ICU Mortality Predictions: a Feasibility Study on the eICU Demo Dataset
evidence.outcome: Guideline grounding of LLM ICU mortality explanations, agentic guideline-checking pipeline vs standalone LLM
evidence.effect: Among 14 overlapping cases, guideline grounding was 0.762 (agentic) vs 0.143 (standalone); 1 standalone explanation had outcome leakage vs none for agentic. Standalone had higher SHAP alignment (Jaccard 0.171 vs 0.077).
evidence.quote: Clinically, the results suggest that agentic decomposition may improve safety-relevant grounding and patient-specific detail, but it should be paired with attribution-based checks before use in high-stakes risk explanation.

evidence.title: MA-RAG: Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Query-Driven Summarization of Longitudinal Parkinson's Disease Assessments
evidence.outcome: Fact precision and hallucination rate of grounded multi-agent RAG versus non-grounded baselines
evidence.effect: MA-RAG increased Fact Precision up to 122% (0.436 to 0.990) and reduced Hallucination Rate by up to 98% (0.564 to 0.010) versus Traditional, RAG-only, and Single-agent RAG baselines.
evidence.quote: Compared to Traditional, RAG-only, and Single-agent RAG baselines, MA-RAG substantially improves factual correctness, achieving up to a 122% relative increase in Fact Precision (from 0.436 to 0.990) and reducing the Hallucination Rate by up to 98% (from 0.564 to 0.010), while consistently receiving top ratings from clinical experts for organization and clinical usefulness.

evidence.title: Review Before Trust: Source-Grounded Integrity Gates for AI-Assisted Personal Health Records
evidence.outcome: Source-grounded admission of generated candidates
evidence.effect: Hardened quotation- and row-level policy admitted 72 of 97 numeric candidates and retained 25 for review; schema validation accepted all 97.
evidence.quote: The reports produce 97 numeric candidates: schema validation accepts all 97, an earlier packet-level evidence check accepts 94, and the hardened quotation- and row-level policy admits 72 while retaining 25 for review.
evidence.sample_unit: numeric candidates extracted from laboratory PDF reports

evidence.title: Improving Health Literacy through Lay Summarization of Radiological Reports: An Evaluation of BioNER and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
evidence.outcome: Quality, factual consistency and readability of lay summaries with versus without retrieval grounding
evidence.effect: RAG alone offered no benefit and could introduce hallucinations from irrelevant retrieved terms; RAG plus NER degraded few-shot performance but improved readability when fine-tuned.
evidence.quote: Results show that NER consistently improves readability and overall quality, while RAG alone offers no benefit and can introduce hallucinations from irrelevant retrieved terms.

evidence.title: EviGen: Predictive Evidence Scaffolding for Verifiable Clinical Rationale Generation
evidence.outcome: Rationale faithfulness and prediction performance of evidence-grounded generation versus full-context LLM and RAG baselines
evidence.effect: EviGen improves prediction performance and rationale faithfulness over full-context LLM and RAG baselines across three medical prediction datasets; clinical reviewers preferred it in a usability evaluation.
evidence.quote: Across three medical prediction datasets, EviGen improves prediction performance and rationale faithfulness over full-context LLM and RAG baselines, and is preferred by clinical reviewers in a usability evaluation.

evidence.title: RiskAgent: Autonomous Medical AI Copilot for Generalist Risk Prediction
evidence.outcome: Risk-prediction accuracy of LLM agent using evidence-based clinical tools versus commercial LLMs without them
evidence.effect: RiskAgent (8B) reached 76.33% accuracy on MedRisk, outperforming o1, o3-mini and GPT-4.5 and doubling GPT-4o's 38.39%.
evidence.quote: The results show that our RiskAgent, with 8 billion model parameters, achieves 76.33% accuracy, outperforming the most recent commercial LLMs, o1, o3-mini, and GPT-4.5, and doubling the 38.39% accuracy of GPT-4o.

evidence.title: Implementing a context-augmented large language model to guide precision cancer medicine
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of biomarker-driven treatment recommendations with vs without retrieval grounding in curated knowledge base
evidence.effect: LLM-only achieved 62–75% accuracy; RAG-LLM achieved 79–91% with an unstructured database and 94–95% with a structured database.
evidence.quote: While LLM-only achieved 62–75% accuracy in biomarker-driven treatment recommendations, RAG-LLM achieved 79–91% accuracy with an unstructured database and 94–95% accuracy with a structured database.

evidence.title: Introducing Answered with Evidence - a framework for evaluating whether LLM responses to biomedical questions are founded in evidence
evidence.outcome: reliable evidence-grounded answers
evidence.effect: Public-information LLMs varied greatly; ensemble agreement was 49%; ensemble plus Alexandria reliable for over 64% of queries.
evidence.quote: Combined, the ensemble approach and the Alexandria custom built source enabled reliable answers to over 64% of biomedical queries.

evidence.title: Accelerating Insight Discovery in Large Biomedical Text with Scalable Processing Framework
evidence.outcome: Accuracy, efficiency, and misinformation risk when LLM answers are grounded in a curated document corpus
evidence.effect: Reported improvements in accuracy, efficiency, and computational cost on benchmark datasets; the curated document approach enhanced reliability and reduced misinformation risk. No numbers given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Comparative evaluations on benchmark datasets demonstrate improvements in accuracy, efficiency, and computational cost, with the curated document approach enhancing reliability and reducing misinformation risk.

evidence.title: Learning the Phenotype of Medical Hallucinations
evidence.outcome: Hallucination rate when outputs are integrated with structured open clinical knowledge plus a classifier
evidence.effect: Hallucinations fell from 31% to 0.3% in Llama-3-70B on oncology trial physician QA; risk driven below accepted clinical error thresholds.
evidence.quote: By systematically driving hallucination risk below accepted clinical error thresholds, CHECK provides a scalable and plug-and-play solution to enable the reliable deployment of LLMs in medicine and other mission-critical domains.

evidence.title: A Comparative Performance Study of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems in Gynecologic Oncology
evidence.outcome: Expert-graded response quality of RAG architectures versus non-RAG baseline on gynecologic oncology questions
evidence.effect: RAG systems generally outperformed non-RAG baseline; largest gains for complex surgical questions, modest and heterogeneous improvements for cervical cancer guideline questions.
evidence.quote: Across domains, RAG systems generally outperformed the non-RAG baseline.

evidence.title: Clinical Large Language Models with Multi-Stage Instruction Tuning and Advanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation
evidence.outcome: Ablation of enhanced RAG components and error analysis of critical errors on medical benchmarks
evidence.effect: Ablation confirmed synergistic contributions of the innovations, and error analysis showed a substantial reduction in critical errors; no numbers given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: An ablation study confirms the synergistic contributions of our innovations, and an error analysis highlights a substantial reduction in critical errors, positioning ECRAG-LLM as a more reliable and intelligent solution for resource-constrained clinical environments.

evidence.title: EviLedger: governing clinical AI with a verifiable evidence ledger
evidence.outcome: Unverifiable citations in LLM retrieval grounded in verified evidence ledger
evidence.effect: Unverifiable citations reduced from 28.4% to 2.3%
evidence.quote: As an auditable memory layer for LLM-based retrieval, EviLedger reduces stale citations from 14.7% to 1.2% and unverifiable citations from 28.4% to 2.3%, while supporting p95 rollback in 5.13 s at 78M assertions.

evidence.title: FHIR-RAG-MEDS: Integrating HL7 FHIR with Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models for Enhanced Medical Decision Support
evidence.outcome: Semantic accuracy, faithfulness to guidelines, and clinical relevance of RAG-grounded vs. medical LLM outputs
evidence.effect: System consistently outperformed state-of-the-art medical LLMs, with higher semantic accuracy, improved faithfulness to guideline content, and stronger clinical relevance (no numbers in abstract).
evidence.quote: The system consistently outperformed state-of-the-art medical LLMs, demonstrating higher semantic accuracy, improved faithfulness to guideline content, and stronger clinical relevance.

evidence.title: Deterministic Retrieval-Grounded Language Models for Clinical Counseling: Large-Scale Multilingual Evaluation with Cryptographically Verifiable Pipelines
evidence.outcome: Effect of retrieval grounding on clinical fidelity in ablation experiments
evidence.effect: Ablation showed retrieval grounding contributes significantly to performance, driving clinical fidelity (English 3.55/5; Chinese 4.73/5 with full system).
evidence.quote: Ablation experiments demonstrate that retrieval grounding and deterministic safety routing each contribute significantly to overall performance, with the former driving clinical fidelity and the latter driving safety.

evidence.title: Enhancing LLM Accuracy and Reducing Hallucinations using Query Refinement Technique and Knowledge Graphs
evidence.outcome: Hallucination reduction and F1 when grounding LLM answers in UMLS knowledge graph versus other LLM methods
evidence.effect: Hallucinations drastically reduced; F1 of 91.1% (MedQA) and 86.0% (custom dataset) with domain-fine-tuned models; KG-validated data with fine-tuned models performed best among LLM methods.
evidence.quote: Evaluating on MedQA and Custom biomedical dataset for various tasks, our method drastically reduced hallucinations and achieved F1 rates of 91.1% (MedQA) and 86.0% (our dataset) with domain-fine-tuned models like Llama-3.1-8B-UltraMedical.

evidence.title: Cosine Similarity Conflates Clinically Distinct Cancer Variants: A Case for Typed-Graph Retrieval in Precision Oncology Decision Support
evidence.outcome: Wrong-variant retrieval rate with exact-ID guardrail or typed-graph retrieval versus cosine retrieval
evidence.effect: Adding an exact variant-ID guardrail to cosine retrieval, and an end-to-end typed-graph pipeline, both reduced wrong-variant retrieval to zero; typed graph had 95.8% normalization accuracy.
evidence.quote: Adding an exact variant-ID guardrail to cosine retrieval, and routing retrieval through an end-to-end typed-graph pipeline, both reduced wrong-variant retrieval to zero.

evidence.title: Extraction of Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) Concepts from Clinical Notes Utilizing Large Language Models (LLM) with Model Context Protocol (MCP)
evidence.outcome: HPO extraction F1, precision, and mapping error rate with vs without real-time ontology retrieval grounding
evidence.effect: Mean F1 rose from 0.46 (SD 0.22) to 0.72 (SD 0.15) (p<0.001); mapping error rate fell from 40.9% to 7.8%; precision rose from 56% to 90%; inferred-phenotype hallucination rate not significantly increased (p=0.08).
evidence.quote: Tool augmentation significantly improved performance across all models.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM extraction runs (>2,000 total, across 4 synthetic clinical genetics notes)

evidence.title: To RAG, or Not to RAG? A Comparative Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for ICD Coding of German Tumor Diagnoses
evidence.outcome: ICD coding accuracy of LLMs with versus without retrieval augmentation from standardized classifications
evidence.effect: RAG improved base LLM performance; Llama 3.3 70B with RAG reached 80.6% partial-match (ICD-10) and 75.0% (ICD-O), beating embedding approaches on partial match but not on exact match.
evidence.quote: RAG improved base LLM performance and outperformed embedding-based approaches on partial-match accuracy (80.6% partial-match accuracy for ICD-10 and 75.0% for ICD-O with Llama 3.3 70B), but not on exact-match accuracy.

evidence.title: Trustworthy agentic genomics through versioned skill libraries
evidence.outcome: Lethal-class pharmacogenomic errors with and without retrieval grounding in guidelines
evidence.effect: Retrieval raised phenotype accuracy but paradoxically increased lethal-class errors; versioned skills executed as code did not increase them. No numbers given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Letting the model reason was stochastic and unsafe, and grounding it in the correct guidelines by retrieval paradoxically increased lethal-class errors.
evidence.sample_unit: scored evaluations (110 pharmacogenomic cases, nine LLMs)

evidence.title: MAP-RAG: A Multi-View Adaptive Pattern-Aware Medical Retrieval-Augmented Generation Diagnostic Framework
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic Top-3 accuracy with versus without external retrieval grounding (ablation)
evidence.effect: MAP-RAG Top-3 accuracy 79.60% general practice, 80.69% ophthalmology, 87.80% internal medicine, outperforming non-retrieval and conventional RAG baselines; removing external retrieval caused the largest declines.
evidence.quote: Ablation analyses showed that removing external retrieval or multi-view deconstruction caused the largest performance declines, indicating that evidence retrieval and structured record decomposition were the main drivers of improvement.

evidence.title: Retrieval-Augmented Claude Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5 Surpass Human Performance on the Nuclear Cardiology Board Preparation Exam (and Claude Drafts a Paper About it)
evidence.outcome: Exam accuracy with retrieval-augmented generation versus no context
evidence.effect: GPT-4o improved from 63.1% without context to 73.8% on text-only questions with textbook context; RAG-enabled Claude Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5 reached 86.3% and 86.7%.
evidence.quote: Providing textbook context improved GPT-4o to 73.8% on text-only questions, but still fell short of human trainees.

evidence.title: Prompt-engineering improves clinical safety of large language models for opioid equipotency conversion
evidence.outcome: Opioid conversion accuracy with reference-table prompt augmentation versus naive prompting
evidence.effect: Reference-based prompt augmentation significantly improved performance, with over half of models achieving high proportions of conversions within tight accuracy for morphine equivalent conversions.
evidence.quote: Reference-based prompt augmentation significantly improved performance, with over half of models achieving high proportions of conversions within tight accuracy for morphine equivalent conversions.

evidence.title: Structured retrieval closes the gap between low-cost and frontier clinical language models
evidence.outcome: NIHSS scoring MAE with structured retrieval versus non-agentic baselines
evidence.effect: MAE fell from 4.58 to 2.96 points (mean gain 1.62; 95% CI 1.57–1.67; 35% relative reduction); tool-retrieved pipelines outperformed RAG in 33 of 36 combinations.
evidence.quote: Structured retrieval reduces mean absolute error (MAE) from 4.58 to 2.96 points relative to non-agentic baselines (mean gain 1.62 MAE points; 95% CI 1.57–1.67; 35% relative reduction), with consistent gains across all 36 stress combinations.
evidence.sample_unit: retained model runs (100 de-identified acute stroke cases x 144 conditions)

evidence.title: A Clinical Guideline-Grounded Hybrid Agentic Framework for Holistic Epilepsy Management
evidence.outcome: Decision reliability of guideline-grounded agentic framework versus LLM-based and task-specific baselines across six epilepsy tasks
evidence.effect: Guideline-grounded generative coordination combined with discriminative evidence gave more reliable and comprehensive decisions than conventional LLM-based and task-specific baselines; no numbers in abstract.
evidence.quote: Results demonstrate that integrating discriminative evidence with guideline-grounded generative coordination yields more reliable and comprehensive decisions compared to conventional LLM-based and task-specific baselines.

evidence.title: TurkishMedLLM: A Source-Grounded and Safety-Aware Turkish Medical LLM for Clinical Decision Support and Digital Health Applications
evidence.outcome: Faithfulness, relevancy and clinical caution of grounded vs ungrounded LLM configurations
evidence.effect: Fine-tuned RAG achieved RAGAS faithfulness 0.91, response relevancy 0.88, DeepEval answer relevancy 0.90, clinical caution 0.93, outperforming base LLM, base RAG, and fine-tuned non-RAG.
evidence.quote: In generation-stage evaluation, the fine-tuned RAG configuration achieved a RAGAS faithfulness score of 0.91, response relevancy of 0.88, DeepEval answer relevancy of 0.90, and clinical caution score of 0.93, outperforming the base LLM, base RAG, and fine-tuned non-RAG configurations.

evidence.title: Small but Specialized: A Domain-Adapted Retrieval-Augmented LLM Outperforms Frontier Generalists in Pediatric and Adolescent Gynecology
evidence.outcome: Ablation of retrieval versus fine-tuning on reference-based and faithfulness metrics
evidence.effect: Retrieval was the dominant performance lever; fine-tuning added further gains in stylistic and faithfulness quality. Full system gained +82% faithfulness over the base model (p<0.001).
evidence.quote: Ablation analysis showed that retrieval was the dominant performance lever, with fine-tuning adding consistent further gains in stylistic and faithfulness quality.

evidence.title: Retrieval‑Augmented Clinical Question‑Answering System for Bariatric Surgery Built on the ASMBS Textbook: From Good to Great
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM answers with vs without textbook-grounded retrieval on bariatric surgery questions
evidence.quote: Textbook-augmented RAG produced consistent and significant accuracy gains across all models.

evidence.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Reducing Hallucinations in Drug-Related Question Answering Systems
evidence.outcome: Hallucination rate, faithfulness and factual accuracy with vs without retrieval grounding
evidence.effect: RAG reduced hallucination rate from 47.8% to 12.3% (74.3% relative reduction); Faithfulness 0.52 to 0.87; Factual Accuracy 0.54 to 0.89.
evidence.quote: Evaluated on a purpose-built dataset of 150 drug-related question–answer pairs spanning ten commonly used medications and multiple information categories, our RAG system reduces the hallucination rate from 47.8% to 12.3% — a 74.3% relative reduction — while improving Faithfulness from 0.52 to 0.87 and Factual Accuracy from 0.54 to 0.89.

evidence.title: Framework for Grounding Healthcare LLMs in a Causal Knowledge Graph: A Cardiovascular Example
evidence.outcome: Effect of knowledge-graph grounding conditions versus ungrounded LLM on causal, evidence, unsupported-claim, and intervention accuracy metrics
evidence.effect: Integrated grounding (C4) had best causal edge F1 0.838, adverse-effect F1 0.833, evidence accuracy 0.738, unsupported claim rate 0.114; ungrounded C1 had highest raw intervention accuracy 0.948 but no measurable grounding.
evidence.quote: The metric panel discriminates conditions along interpretable, non-redundant axes: C4 obtains the strongest causal edge F1 (0.838), adverse-effect F1 (0.833), evidence accuracy (0.738), and unsupported claim rate (0.114), while C1 obtains the highest raw intervention accuracy (0.948) with no measurable causal or evidential grounding.

evidence.title: OncoGenRAG: Evidence-Grounded Retrieval and BioBERT Classification for Precision Oncology Variant Interpretation
evidence.outcome: Hallucination rate of evidence-grounded retrieval system versus ungrounded baseline on 100 clinical-style queries
evidence.effect: No hallucinated answer observed with grounding (100% database grounding) versus a 41.0% no-hallucination rate for the ungrounded baseline; internal validation only.
evidence.quote: No hallucinated answer was observed under the study’s operational definition, compared with a 41.0% no-hallucination rate for the ungrounded baseline.

evidence.title: Evaluating Clinical Concept Extraction and Evidence-Bounded Terminology Linking: Multisite Model Comparison and Pilot Ablation Study
evidence.outcome: Reference-matched linking of known-concept spans under complete retrieval versus masked retrieval versus LLM-only inference
evidence.effect: Complete retrieval linked 28/28 known-concept spans (100%; 95% CI 87.9%-100%); masking assigned POSSIBLE_CANDIDATES to all 28; LLM-only linked 3/28 (10.7%).
evidence.quote: In Study 2, complete retrieval returned a reference-matched link for 28/28 known-concept spans (100%; 95% CI, 87.9%-100%).
evidence.sample_unit: deidentified clinical notes (Study 1); 56 clinical spans (Study 2); 84 terms (Study 3)

evidence.title: TrialCode Agent: LLM-Assisted Clinical Code-Set Construction for Trial Emulation
evidence.outcome: Exact-code F1 of code-set generation with vs without hybrid biomedical retrieval grounding
evidence.effect: Hybrid RAG improved aggregate F1 only for Qwen; increased GPT-5.5 RxNorm F1 from 0.320 to 0.909; did not consistently improve exact-code performance.
evidence.quote: Hybrid biomedical RAG improved aggregate F1 only for Qwen but increased GPT-5.5 RxNorm F1 from 0.320 to 0.909.

evidence.title: A Knowledge Graph-Based Intelligent Guidance System for Competency-Oriented Anesthesiology Residency Training: Design and Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Guideline compliance and factual consistency of RAG-grounded answers versus standalone LLM on 300-question benchmark
evidence.effect: Dual-engine RAG: 98.5% guideline compliance, 97.8% factual consistency; standalone LLM 81.4% guideline compliance; single-vector RAG 93.7%.
evidence.quote: The dual-engine RAG framework yielded a guideline compliance rate of 98.5% and factual consistency of 97.8%, outperforming standalone large language models (81.4% guideline compliance) and single-vector RAG approaches (93.7%).

evidence.title: Natural Language Processing and Large Language Model-Based Automated AO/OTA Classification of Proximal Femoral Fractures: A MIMIC-IV Retrospective Study
evidence.outcome: AO/OTA 31A vs 31B classification accuracy with RAG grounding versus zero-shot and few-shot prompting
evidence.effect: RAG accuracy 94.29% (F1 94.29%) equaled zero-shot 94.29% (F1 94.28%); few-shot dropped to 88.57% (F1 88.53%). RAG showed no measurable advantage in binary classification.
evidence.quote: Zero‑shot prompting attained the same accuracy (94.29%, F1 = 94.28%), while few‑shot learning unexpectedly dropped to 88.57% (F1 = 88.53%).

evidence.title: Evaluating approaches of training a generative large language model for multi-label classification of unstructured electronic health records
evidence.outcome: multi-label EHR classification performance
evidence.effect: RAG improved performance only in few-shot learning; few-shot with RAG outperformed zero-shot with RAG, but showed no significant difference compared to zero-shot with PEFT.
evidence.quote: Notably, PEFT significantly enhances model performance in both zero-shot and few-shot learning; however, RAG improves performance only in few-shot learning.

evidence.title: Multimodal Large Language Model Passes Specialty Board Examination and Surpasses Human Test-Taker Scores: A Comparative Analysis Examining the Stepwise Impact of Model Prompting Strategies on Performance
evidence.outcome: Exam accuracy with stepwise prompting strategies including retrieval-augmented generation versus baseline
evidence.effect: All strategies combined (prompt engineering, RAG, five-shot, AVRM) raised GPT-4 from 60.3% to 80.7% and Gemini Pro from 48.0% to 54.3%; RAG-specific effect not given in abstract.
evidence.quote: Implementing all prompting strategies improved the overall score of GPT-4 from 60.3% to 80.7% and Gemini Pro’s from 48.0% to 54.3%.

evidence.title: Biomedical Text Normalization through Generative Modeling
evidence.outcome: Normalization accuracy (mean shortest SNOMED path length) of retrieval-grounded versus ungrounded LLM strategies
evidence.effect: RAGnorm was most effective on every dataset: mean shortest path length 0.21 (oncology), 0.58 (sampled), 0.90 (top terms). Micro F1 88.01 on TAC2017 task 4, surpassing all other models.
evidence.quote: We found that RAGnorm was the most effective throughout each dataset, achieving a mean shortest path length of 0.21 for the domain-specific dataset, 0.58 for the sampled dataset, and 0.90 for the top terms dataset.

evidence.title: Towards Evaluating the Diagnostic Ability of LLMs
evidence.outcome: Missed ground-truth diagnoses with and without RAG grounding
evidence.effect: Top models missed 0.5% of ground truth conditions clearly inferable from data; RAG further improved this error rate to 0.2%.
evidence.quote: We found that GPT-4o from OpenAI and Claude Sonnet 3.5 from Anthropic were the top performers with them only missing 0.5% of ground truth conditions that were clearly inferable from the available data; RAG further improved this error rate to 0.2%.

evidence.title: ChatDoctor: A Medical Chat Model Fine-Tuned on a Large Language Model Meta-AI (LLaMA) Using Medical Domain Knowledge
evidence.outcome: Response accuracy with versus without self-directed retrieval from online and offline sources
evidence.effect: Authors report substantial improvements in response accuracy when the model was equipped with self-directed information retrieval; no numbers given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: By equipping the model with self-directed information retrieval from reliable online and offline sources, we observed substantial improvements in the accuracy of its responses.

evidence.title: Generative artificial intelligence and non-pharmacological bias: an experimental study on cancer patient sexual health communications
evidence.outcome: guideline grounding effect on intervention recommendations
evidence.effect: Guideline-sourced Bot2 still favored consultation over pharmacological interventions, OR 97.2 (p<0.001); Bot1 OR 47.3 (p<0.001).
evidence.quote: Despite the lack of reflection on guideline recommendations, 'consultation' was significantly more prevalent in both bots' responses compared with pharmacological interventions, with ORs of 47.3 (p<0.001) in Bot1 and 97.2 (p<0.001) in Bot2.

evidence.title: Evaluating and Enhancing Large Language Models' Performance in Domain-Specific Medicine: Development and Usability Study With DocOA
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of RAG-grounded DocOA versus ungrounded GPT-3.5/GPT-4 on osteoarthritis benchmark
evidence.effect: Overall benchmark accuracy 0.88 for DocOA vs 0.24 for GPT-4 and 0.16 for GPT-3.5 (P<.001); human-rated inaccuracy 19.3% vs 50% and 57%.
evidence.quote: The rate of inaccuracy was the highest for GPT-3.5 (57%, n=1200), followed by GPT-4 and DocOA at 50% (n=1200) and 19.3% (n=1200), respectively.
evidence.sample_unit: benchmark questions (337 guideline-item, 145 management-option, 216 treatment-strategy, 80 real-case QA)

evidence.title: GastroBot: a Chinese gastrointestinal disease chatbot based on the retrieval-augmented generation
evidence.outcome: Faithfulness, context recall, answer relevance of RAG-grounded chatbot; manual comparison with other models
evidence.effect: Context recall 95%, faithfulness to source 93.73%, answer relevance 92.28%; manual assessment showed GastroBot delivered more valuable knowledge with completeness and consistency than other models.
evidence.quote: During manual assessment of GastroBot, in comparison with other models, our GastroBot model delivers a substantial amount of valuable knowledge while ensuring the completeness and consistency of the results.

evidence.title: ChatENT: Augmented Large Language Model for Expert Knowledge Retrieval in Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.venue: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.outcome: Error rate and hallucinations of retrieval-grounded ChatENT versus base ChatGPT4.0 on OHNS exam questions
evidence.effect: ChatENT outperformed ChatGPT4.0 with 58.4% (Canadian Royal College sample questions) and 26.0% (US board practice questions) error reduction; fewer hallucinations and greater consistency.
evidence.quote: ChatENT showed enhanced performance in the analysis and interpretation of OHNS information, outperforming ChatGPT4.0 in both the Canadian Royal College OHNS sample examination questions challenge and the US board practice questions challenge, with a 58.4% and 26.0% error reduction, respectively.

evidence.title: Development and Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model Framework for Ophthalmology
evidence.outcome: Alignment with scientific consensus of retrieval-augmented LLM versus baseline LLM
evidence.effect: Consensus improved from 46.5% to 84.0% (difference 37.5%; 95% CI 29.0%-46.0%; P<.001); not different from GPT-4 (79.2%).
evidence.quote: Our LLM surpassed the baseline model in aligning with scientific consensus, improving consensus from 46.5% to 84.0% (difference = 37.5%; 95% CI, 29.0%-46.0%; P < .001) and not different from GPT-4 with a value of 79.2% (difference = 4.8%; 95% CI, −0.3% to 10.0%; P = .06).

evidence.title: Improving accuracy of GPT-3/4 results on biomedical data using a retrieval-augmented language model
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and hallucination rate of retrieval-grounded RAG vs general LLMs on DLBCL questions
evidence.effect: RAG had highest mean accuracy (2.46 vs GPT-4 2.26, GPT-3.5 1.82, Prometheus 1.74) and fewest answers with hallucinations (3/19 vs GPT-3.5 13/19, GPT-4 8/19).
evidence.quote: Overall, the RAG model enhanced with domain specific data outperformed other LLMs with respect to accuracy and relevance of answers, and produced answers with the fewest observed hallucinations.

evidence.title: Assessing the utility of large language models for phenotype-driven gene prioritization in the diagnosis of rare genetic disease
evidence.outcome: Gene prediction accuracy with versus without retrieval-augmented generation and few-shot learning
evidence.effect: RAG and few-shot learning did not improve gene prediction accuracy; best model GPT-4 reached 17.0% top-50 accuracy.
evidence.quote: Advanced techniques such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and few-shot learning did not improve the accuracy.

evidence.title: RDguru: A Conversational Intelligent Agent for Rare Diseases
evidence.venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
evidence.outcome: Alignment of generated answers with authoritative knowledge, retrieval-augmented agent versus ChatGPT
evidence.effect: RDguru outperformed ChatGPT in generating descriptions aligned with authoritative knowledge, measured by ROUGE scores, GPT-4-based automatic rating, and RAGAs metrics.
evidence.quote: A multi-aspect Q&A analysis demonstrates RDguru outperforms ChatGPT in generating descriptions aligned with authoritative knowledge, quantified by ROUGE scores, GPT-4-based automatic rating, and RAGAs evaluation metrics.

evidence.title: Ascle-A Python Natural Language Processing Toolkit for Medical Text Generation: Development and Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: ROUGE-L of RAG-grounded question answering versus vanilla LLMs
evidence.effect: RAG framework with knowledge graph and ranking raised ROUGE-L by 18% over vanilla models; physician-rated accuracy 3.90/5 and completeness 3.31/5.
evidence.quote: In the question-answering task, the RAG framework raised the ROUGE-L score by 18% over the vanilla models.

evidence.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models in Evidence-Based Medicine
evidence.venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
evidence.outcome: PICO extraction performance with knowledge-guided prompting versus zero-shot
evidence.effect: Knowledge-guided prompting improved GPT-4 performance by 13.10% over zero-shot in PICO extraction.
evidence.quote: Promoting strategies such as knowledge-guided prompting proved highly effective (e.g., improving the performance of GPT-4 by 13.10% over zero-shot in PICO extraction).
evidence.sample_unit: benchmark tasks (PICO extraction, biomedical QA, RCT summarization, text simplification)

evidence.title: Custom Large Language Models Improve Accuracy: Comparing Retrieval Augmented Generation and Artificial Intelligence Agents to Noncustom Models for Evidence-Based Medicine
evidence.venue: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy on ACL guideline questions with versus without RAG grounding
evidence.effect: All noncustom LLMs started below 60% accuracy; RAG improved every model's accuracy by an average 39.7%; best RAG model Llama3 70b reached 94%.
evidence.quote: Applying RAG improved the accuracy of every model by an average 39.7%.

evidence.title: Research on a traditional Chinese medicine case-based question-answering system integrating large language models and knowledge graphs
evidence.outcome: Rater-scored safety, usability and smoothness of knowledge-graph-grounded QA versus the same LLMs without RAG
evidence.effect: Safety 2.868 vs 1.57-1.74 and usability 2.848 vs 1.55-1.67 for LLMs without RAG; smoothness 2.98 vs 2.13-2.21 (3-point scale, 5 TCM evaluators, 20 questions). RAGAS faithfulness 0.9375.
evidence.quote: Overall, the traditional Chinese medicine case-based Q&A system, based on LLMs and knowledge graphs, provides outstanding performance in terms of security, professionalism, and fluency, significantly outperforming traditional Q&A systems that rely solely on LLMs, and has enormous potential for application.

evidence.title: Boosting GPT models for genomics analysis: generating trusted genetic variant annotations and interpretations through RAG and Fine-tuning
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of genetic variant annotations from RAG grounding versus fine-tuning
evidence.effect: RAG with 190 million curated variant annotations gave accurate annotations and outperformed fine-tuning on data volume, accuracy and cost. Fine-tuning improved only some fields, and accuracy across more fields remained suboptimal.
evidence.quote: Our project also revealed that RAG outperforms fine-tuning in factual knowledge injection in terms of data volume, accuracy, and cost-effectiveness.

evidence.title: Leveraging Medical Knowledge Graphs Into Large Language Models for Diagnosis Prediction: Design and Application Study
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic prediction accuracy of LLM with versus without knowledge graph retrieved paths
evidence.effect: DR.KNOWS with KG paths showed higher accuracy in extracting diagnostic concepts and improved diagnostic prediction metrics over QuickUMLS, T5 and ChatGPT baselines; prompt-tuned T5 with KG paths achieved highest ROUGE-L and CUI F1.
evidence.quote: Prompt-based fine-tuning of Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer with DR.KNOWS knowledge paths achieved the highest ROUGE-L (Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation-Longest Common Subsequence) and concept unique identifier F<sub>1</sub>-scores, highlighting the benefits of KG integration.

evidence.title: From RAGs to riches: Utilizing large language models to write documents for clinical trials
evidence.outcome: Clinical thinking/logic score of generated protocol sections, RAG vs off-the-shelf GPT-4
evidence.effect: RAG-augmented LLM scored about twice as high on clinical thinking and logic; eligibility criteria ~33% to ~86%, endpoints ~50% to ~73%; only this dimension survived Bonferroni correction.
evidence.quote: However, the RAG-augmented LLM substantially outperforms the off-the-shelf LLM in terms of clinical thinking and logic , where the output of the RAG-augmented LLM scores approximately twice as high as the off-the-shelf LLM.

evidence.title: Retrieval-augmented generation enhances large language model performance on the Japanese orthopedic board examination
evidence.venue: Journal of orthopaedic science : official journal of the Japanese Orthopaedic Association
evidence.outcome: Exam accuracy with versus without retrieval-augmented generation from an orthopedic textbook database
evidence.effect: GPT-4o rose from 62% to 72% and o1-preview from 67% to 84% with RAG. GPT-3.5 Turbo showed no improvement (29% to 28%).
evidence.quote: GPT-4o rose from 62 % to 72 %, while o1-preview increased from 67 % to 84 %.

evidence.title: AtlasGPT: a language model grounded in neurosurgery with domain-specific data and document retrieval
evidence.outcome: Accuracy, robustness to misinformation, and hallucination for grounded (fine-tuned plus retrieval) LLM versus general LLMs
evidence.effect: AtlasGPT was fooled 14% of the time in adversarial misinformation testing versus 44% for GPT-4 and 68% for Gemini Advanced. Accuracy was 96% versus 88% and 93%. No hallucination was found.
evidence.quote: In adversarial testing, under which AtlasGPT was tasked with identifying medical misinformation, it was fooled 14% of the time, compared with 44% for GPT-4 and 68% for Gemini Advanced.

evidence.title: Semantic Clinical Artificial Intelligence vs Native Large Language Model Performance on the USMLE
evidence.outcome: USMLE question accuracy of Llama models with vs without semantic clinical knowledge RAG
evidence.effect: SCAI RAG significantly improved 13B on Steps 1 and 3, 70B on Step 2, 405B on Step 3; 13B with RAG passed Step 3 (60.2%). 70B and 405B passed all steps with or without RAG.
evidence.quote: Significant improvements associated with SCAI RAG were found for the 13B model on Steps 1 and 3, the 70B model on Step 2, and the 405B parameter model on Step 3.

evidence.title: AI-driven personalized nutrition: RAG-based digital health solution for obesity and type 2 diabetes
evidence.outcome: Adherence of RAG-generated recipes to health guidelines and sustainability criteria
evidence.effect: 80.1% adherence to health guidelines (calories, fiber, fats) and 92% compliance with sustainability criteria across 1,000 recipes; no non-RAG comparator reported.
evidence.quote: In evaluating 1,000 recipes, the system achieved 80.1% adherence to health guidelines meeting targets for calories, fiber, and fats and 92% compliance with sustainability criteria, emphasizing seasonal and locally sourced ingredients.

evidence.title: Comparison of Large Language Models' Performance on 600 Nuclear Medicine Technology Board Examination-Style Questions
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLMs on nuclear medicine board-style questions with versus without retrieval-augmented generation
evidence.effect: With RAG, top OpenAI models reached 0.787 and 0.783 overall accuracy; Anthropic Opus 0.773 and Gemini 1.5 Pro 0.750 with RAG; RAG increased accuracy of an off-the-shelf model.
evidence.quote: This study also demonstrates that adding a RAG workflow can increase the accuracy of an off-the-shelf model.
evidence.sample_unit: nuclear medicine technology board examination-style questions

evidence.title: Benchmarking large language models GPT-4o, llama 3.1, and qwen 2.5 for cancer genetic variant classification
evidence.outcome: Effect of retrieval-augmented generation on variant classification accuracy
evidence.effect: Prompt engineering significantly improved accuracy, while RAG further enhanced performance. Accuracy of GPT-4o in distinguishing clinically relevant variants from VUS was 0.7318 (baseline).
evidence.quote: Prompt engineering significantly improved accuracy, while retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) further enhanced performance.

evidence.title: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT-4 for Automated Mapping of Local Medical Terminologies to SNOMED CT
evidence.venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
evidence.outcome: Valid SNOMED CT term match and exact match rates for RAG-grounded versus other GPT-4 mapping approaches
evidence.effect: RAG had 96.2% valid term match and 57.6% exact match, versus fine-tuned 69.2% valid and 47.2% exact; RAG structural errors were 14%, lower than other models.
evidence.quote: The RAG model achieved the highest performance with a 96.2% valid SNOMED CT term match rate and a 57.6% overall exact match rate, surpassing the fine-tuned model (69.2% valid term match, 47.2% exact match).

evidence.title: CMedRAGBot: A Chinese Medical Chatbot Based on Graph RAG and Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Exam question accuracy of LLMs with versus without knowledge-graph RAG grounding
evidence.effect: Integrating CMedRAGBot (graph RAG) significantly improved test accuracy of all five LLMs, with increases of up to approximately 10%.
evidence.quote: The results indicate that the integration of CMedRAGBot significantly improves the test accuracy of all models, with increases of up to approximately 10%.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence for solving pediatric clinical cases: A Retrieval-Augmented approach utilizing Llama3.2 and structured references
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on pediatric multiple-choice questions with vs without retrieval grounding in Nelson Textbook
evidence.effect: RAG-integrated Llama3.2 achieved 67.78% (1,161/1,713) vs 46.18% (791/1,713) for standalone Llama3.2 (p = 1.5e-112); improvement consistent across pediatric subspecialties.
evidence.quote: The RAG-integrated system significantly outperformed standalone Llama3.2, achieving an overall accuracy of 67.78 % (1,161/1,713) compared to 46.18 % (791/1,713) for Llama3.2 alone (p = 1.5e-112).

evidence.title: Specialized Artificial Intelligence Clinical Decision Support System for Aesthetic Surgery: Aesthetic Surgery Using Retrieval Augmentation (AURA)
evidence.outcome: Faithfulness of RAG-grounded outputs to source literature across 14 scenarios
evidence.effect: Mean faithfulness 0.94, answer relevancy 0.86, factual correctness 0.77; performance stronger for established techniques and safety than emerging procedures.
evidence.quote: AURA demonstrated exceptional performance with mean scores of 0.94 for faithfulness, 0.86 for answer relevancy, and 0.77 for factual correctness.

evidence.title: From text to data: Open-source large language models in extracting cancer related medical attributes from German pathology reports
evidence.outcome: Extraction performance with versus without RAG-enhanced few-shot prompting
evidence.effect: Few-shot prompting improved baseline accuracy and RAG further enhanced performance, particularly for models under 24B parameters; Mistral Small 24B with RAG nearly matched Llama 70B (F1 > 0.90).
evidence.quote: Prompting strategy significantly impacted performance: few-shot prompting improved baseline accuracy, and RAG further enhanced performance, particularly for models with fewer than 24B parameters.

evidence.title: Specialized AI and neurosurgeons in niche expertise: a proof-of-concept in neuromodulation with vagus nerve stimulation
evidence.outcome: Hallucinations and precision of RAG-grounded LLM answers using curated VNS publication knowledge base
evidence.effect: Grounded in 125 curated VNS publications; perfect precision and specificity with no hallucinations detected.
evidence.quote: Confusion matrices revealed higher true correct and true incorrect rates for AI, demonstrating perfect precision and specificity scores with no hallucinations detected.

evidence.title: Development and evaluation of an agentic LLM based RAG framework for evidence-based patient education
evidence.outcome: PEM generation quality with vs without RAG grounding across 12 LLMs
evidence.effect: ARAG-enabled setups (3 and 4) yielded the highest scores for 10 of the 12 models; ARAG positively contributed for most models.
evidence.quote: Based on the resulting scores, the top 5 experiments were identified.
evidence.sample_unit: patient education questions (12 LLMs x 4 setups); 50 PEMs for validation agent test

evidence.title: Assessing and enhancing the reliability of Chinese large language models in dental implantology
evidence.outcome: Change in recall and hallucination rate after long-text modeling for Qwen 2.5
evidence.effect: LTM raised recall by 0.1119 ± 0.2000 (P < 0.05) and lowered hallucination rate by 0.2985 ± 0.4220 (P < 0.05).
evidence.quote: Long-text modeling (LTM) significantly enhanced recall by 0.1119 ± 0.2000 (P < 0.05) and reduced hallucination rate by 0.2985 ± 0.4220 (P < 0.05).

evidence.title: Swedish Medical LLM Benchmark: development and evaluation of a framework for assessing large language models in the Swedish medical domain
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on Swedish clinical knowledge questions with versus without retrieval-augmented generation
evidence.effect: Hybrid RAG systems improved accuracy for clinical knowledge questions; no numeric effect size in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Hybrid systems incorporating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improved accuracy for clinical knowledge questions, highlighting promising directions for safe implementation.

evidence.title: Rapidly Benchmarking Large Language Models for Diagnosing Comorbid Patients: Comparative Study Leveraging the LLM-as-a-Judge Method
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic hit rate of GPT-4o with versus without retrieval-augmented generation using ABIM reference ranges
evidence.effect: RAG significantly improved GPT-4o 05-13 hit rate by an average of 0.8% (P<.006)
evidence.quote: Finally, RAG significantly improved the hit rate of GPT-4o 05-13 by an average of 0.8% (P<.006).

evidence.title: Evaluating Retrieval Augmented Generation-enhanced Large Language Models for Question Answering On German Neurovascular Guidelines
evidence.outcome: Answer correctness of LLM with versus without RAG grounding in guidelines

evidence.quote: Using RAG, GPT-4-turbo's accuracy increased by 11.54% on BCSC and by 10.96% on OphthoQuestions.

evidence.quote: DrugGPT outperforms a wide range of existing LLMs and achieves state-of-the-art performance across all metrics with fewer parameters than generic LLMs.

evidence.title: Leveraging Electronic Health Record Data and Up-to-Date Clinical Guidelines for High-Accuracy Clinical Diabetes Drug and Dosage Recommendation

evidence.title: AcuKG: a comprehensive knowledge graph for medical acupuncture

evidence.effect: Integrating AcuKG improved accuracy: GPT-4o 46% to 54% (P = .03); LLaMA 3 17% to 28% (P = .01)
