evidence.title: MEGA-RAG: a retrieval-augmented generation framework with multi-evidence guided answer refinement for mitigating hallucinations of LLMs in public health
evidence.outcome: Hallucination rate and accuracy of LLM with evidence retrieval grounding versus standalone LLM and standard RAG
evidence.effect: MEGA-RAG reduced hallucination rates by over 40% versus baselines; highest accuracy 0.7913, precision 0.7541, recall 0.8304, F1 0.7904.
evidence.quote: Experimental evaluation demonstrates that MEGA-RAG outperforms four baseline models [PubMedBERT, PubMedGPT, standalone LLM, and LLM with standard retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)], achieving a reduction in hallucination rates by over 40%.

evidence.title: Compliance and factuality of large language models for clinical research document generation
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Regulatory compliance and factual accuracy of ICFs with retrieval-augmented pipeline vs baseline LLMs
evidence.effect: Baseline LLMs (e.g., GPT-4o) achieved 70%-80% compliance with factual errors in 18%-43% of cases; InformGen (retrieval-augmented, human-in-the-loop) achieved nearly 100% compliance and over 90% factual accuracy.
evidence.quote: In contrast, InformGen substantially improved outputs, achieving nearly 100% regulatory compliance and over 90% factual accuracy, as validated by 5 domain-expert annotators.

evidence.title: Evaluating Web Retrieval-Assisted Large Language Models With and Without Whitelisting for Evidence-Based Neurology: Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Correct-answer rate of web-RAG LLMs with vs without whitelisting retrieval to authoritative neurology domains
evidence.effect: Correct rates open vs whitelisted: Sonar 60% vs 78%, Sonar-Pro 80% vs 88%, Sonar-Reasoning-Pro 81% vs 89%; mean accuracy gains 0.23, 0.08, 0.08 on 0-2 scale.
evidence.quote: Restricting retrieval to authoritative neurology domains yielded a clinically meaningful 8 to 18 percentage-point gain in correctness and halved output variability, upgrading a consumer search assistant to a decision-support-level tool that at least performed on par with a specialized literature engine.

evidence.title: Performance of Large Language Models on the Acute Coronary Syndrome Guidelines Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM answers to ACS guideline questions with versus without RAG grounding
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o rose from 71.1% without RAG to 92.1% with RAG (P = 0.017); DeepSeek R1 with RAG reached 94.7% versus 78.9% without RAG.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o without RAG achieved 71.1% accuracy (95% CI: 55.2%-83.0%), which significantly improved with RAG (P = 0.017).

evidence.title: DietAI24 as a framework for comprehensive nutrition estimation using multimodal large language models
evidence.outcome: Nutrient estimation error (MAE) of MLLM grounded via RAG in FNDDS versus commercial and computer vision baselines
evidence.effect: 63% reduction in MAE for food weight and four key nutrients versus existing methods on real-world mixed dishes (p < 0.05); 65 nutrients estimated.
evidence.quote: DietAI24 demonstrates that integrating MLLMs with RAG and standardized nutrition databases can substantially improve dietary assessment accuracy while enabling comprehensive nutrient analysis.

evidence.title: Challenges and Solutions in Applying Large Language Models to Guideline-Based Management Planning and Automated Medical Coding in Health Care: Algorithm Development and Validation
evidence.outcome: Correctness of references, no duplication, formatting, and clinical appropriateness of guideline-grounded management plans
evidence.effect: 62 of 63 outputs (98.4%) met all criteria; the only exception was a minor ordering inconsistency in one repetition of case 14.
evidence.quote: Across the 63 outputs, 62 (98.4%) satisfied all evaluation criteria, with the only exception being a minor ordering inconsistency in one repetition of case 14.
evidence.sample_unit: admissions (MIMIC-IV) for GAVS; 21 clinical test cases for GARAG

evidence.title: Challenges and Solutions in Applying Large Language Models to Guideline-Based Management Planning and Automated Medical Coding in Health Care: Algorithm Development and Validation
evidence.outcome: ICD-10 subcategory recall for vector-search-constrained coding versus unconstrained direct LLM
evidence.effect: Subcategory recall was 20.63% (18.62% weighted) for GAVS versus 17.95% (15.86% weighted) for the vanilla LLM, P<.001; category-level recall was equal (32.60% vs 32.58%, P=.99).
evidence.quote: At the subcategory level, the vanilla LLM achieved 17.95% average recall (15.86% weighted), while GAVS achieved 20.63% (18.62% weighted), a statistically significant improvement (P<.001).
evidence.sample_unit: admissions (MIMIC-IV) for GAVS; 21 clinical test cases for GARAG

evidence.title: RAG-Enhanced Open SLMs for Hypertension Management Chatbots
evidence.outcome: G-Eval medical faithfulness of SLM answers with RAG versus role-playing or full-context prompts
evidence.effect: RAG outperformed or tied the best SLM-only approach for all models; significant for Gemma 3 (4.48 vs 3.48, p=0.0012) and Qwen 2.5 with Mxbai, and Gemma 3 and SmolLM2 with Nomic; no clear pattern in physician ratings.
evidence.quote: Overall, we can observe that the performance of SLMs are indeed positively affected by the RAG pipeline, and for some models the difference is statistically significant.

evidence.title: Enhancing Large Language Models With AI Agents for Chronic Gastritis Management: Comprehensive Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Answer quality of retrieval- and search-grounded agent versus plain LLM on high-complexity questions
evidence.effect: Embedding average score on high-complexity questions was 82.849 for AI agents vs 77.825 for LLMs; agents were particularly effective in clinical consultation tasks.
evidence.quote: Using a dual-evaluation framework comprising automated metrics and expert manual assessments, our results demonstrated that AI agents substantially outperformed LLMs in addressing high-complexity questions (embedding average score: 82.849 for AI agents vs 77.825 for LLMs) and were particularly effective in clinical consultation tasks.

evidence.title: RadOncRAG: A Novel Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework Improves Large Language Model Benchmark Performance in Radiation Oncology
evidence.outcome: Exam accuracy of LLMs with versus without radiation oncology retrieval-augmented generation
evidence.effect: RAG improved nonreasoning models (Gemini-2.0 +6.7% to 79.2%, Llama-3-70b +8.4% to 75.8%, GPT-4o +5.7% to 85.6%); top reasoning models showed no improvement or detriment.
evidence.quote: Gemini-2.0 improved 6.7% (to 79.2%), Llama-3-70b 8.4% (to 75.8%), and GPT-4o 5.7% (to 85.6%) with RAG.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence reliability in implant dentistry: A comparative analysis of clinical accuracy and hallucination patterns across multiple language models
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and fabrication rates of retrieval-augmented vs conventional LLMs on implant dentistry questions
evidence.effect: RAG systems ScholarQA and OpenEvidence achieved 80.0% accuracy with 0% fabrication, while GPT-4o showed 82% reference and 85.7% statistical fabrication.
evidence.quote: ScholarQA and OpenEvidence both achieved high accuracy (80.0%) with 0% fabrication, while GPT-4o showed high rates of reference (82%) and statistical (85.7%) fabrication.

evidence.title: MedSumGraph: enhancing GraphRAG for medical QA with summarization and optimized prompts
evidence.outcome: Medical QA benchmark accuracy of a graph-based retrieval-grounded LLM system versus closed-source and domain-specific LLMs
evidence.effect: Competitive performance on two of eight multiple-choice medical QA benchmarks, including MedQA (USMLE), outperforming closed-source LLMs and domain-specific foundation models; gains on open-domain QA truthfulness.
evidence.quote: MedSumGraph achieves competitive performance on two out of eight multiple-choice medical QA benchmarks, including MedQA (USMLE), outperforming closed-source LLMs and domain-specific foundation models.

evidence.title: Enhancing Large Language Models for Improved Accuracy and Safety in Medical Question Answering: Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Accuracy and hallucination rates of LLMs with vs without retrieval-augmented grounding (Med-RISE)
evidence.effect: Med-RISE raised accuracy 9.8% to 16.3% (mean 13%) across 4 datasets and reduced hallucinations 11.8% to 18% (mean 15.1%); factuality hallucinations down 13.5%, faithfulness down 5.8%.
evidence.quote: The integration of Med-RISE with each LLM led to a substantial increase in accuracy, with improvements ranging from 9.8% to 16.3% (mean 13%, SD 2.3%) across the 4 datasets.

evidence.title: Advancing Chinese Conversation-based Patient Guidance with a Benchmark and Knowledge-Evolvable Assistant
evidence.venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
evidence.outcome: Department-guidance accuracy of LLMs with versus without retrieval augmentation from experience bank and medical knowledge base
evidence.effect: KEA, which adds retrieval-augmented experience, reflection banks and an external medical knowledge base, consistently and significantly boosted CCPG performance of all tested LLMs; best results still fall short of clinical expectations.
evidence.quote: Experiments show that KEA consistently and significantly boosts the CCPG performance of all tested LLMs on PG-Bench.

evidence.title: Nursing Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Retrieval augmented generation for nursing question answering with large language models
evidence.outcome: Answer accuracy and ROUGE-L with vs without retrieval grounding on nursing questions
evidence.quote: For ChatGLM2-6B, ROUGE-L increased from (30.73 ± 1.48) % to (64.27 ± 0.27) %, and accuracy increased from (49.08 ± 0.92) % to (75.83 ± 0.35) %.

evidence.title: Multi-step retrieval and reasoning improves radiology question answering with large language models
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy with multi-step retrieval grounding versus zero-shot and conventional online RAG
evidence.effect: RaR improved mean diagnostic accuracy vs zero-shot (75% vs. 67%; P = 1.1e-7) and vs conventional online RAG (75% vs. 69%; P = 1.9e-6). Reduced hallucinations, with clinically relevant evidence in 46% of cases.
evidence.quote: RaR significantly improved mean diagnostic accuracy versus zero-shot prompting (75% vs. 67%; P = 1.1 × 10<sup>-7</sup>) and conventional online RAG (75% vs. 69%; P = 1.9 × 10<sup>-6</sup>).

evidence.title: Medical QA dialogue datasets in RAG systems performance evaluation and ChatGPT optimization
evidence.outcome: Generation quality (ROUGE-1-f, BERTScore_F1) with retrieval grounding vs direct prompting
evidence.effect: Dialogue-based retrieval significantly improved generation quality relative to direct prompting (ROUGE-1-f: +12.6%, BERTScore_F1: +1.5%, p < 0.05).
evidence.quote: Experimental results show that dialogue-based retrieval significantly improves generation quality relative to direct prompting (e.g., ROUGE-1-f: +12.6%, BERTScore_F1: +1.5%, p < 0.05).

evidence.title: A self-correcting Agentic Graph RAG for clinical decision support in hepatology
evidence.outcome: Faithfulness, context recall and answer relevancy of knowledge-graph-grounded agentic RAG versus GPT-4, standard RAG and Graph RAG
evidence.effect: Agentic Graph RAG scored faithfulness 0.94, context recall 0.92, answer relevancy 0.91, and outperformed GPT-4, standard RAG, and Graph RAG across all metrics.
evidence.quote: It significantly outperformed baseline models (including GPT-4, standard RAG, and Graph RAG) across all evaluation metrics.

evidence.title: GraphRAG-Enabled Local Large Language Model for Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Development of a Proof-of-Concept
evidence.outcome: Response similarity to reference answers (BLEU, Jaccard, BERTScore) for GraphRAG-grounded LLM versus ungrounded LLMs
evidence.effect: GraphRAG local LLM scored BLEU 0.99, Jaccard 0.98, BERTScore 0.98, outperforming ChatGPT, Claude and BioMistral on simulated clinical and layperson prompts.
evidence.quote: It achieved a bilingual evaluation understudy score of 0.99, Jaccard similarity of 0.98, and BERTScore of 0.98, outperforming the benchmark LLMs.

evidence.title: Tumor Board-Inspired Multiagent Artificial Intelligence System for Interpreting Oncology Guidelines

evidence.effect: Guideline-grounded system 90% accuracy vs GPT-4o 48%, Claude 3.7 49%, Gemini 2.5 50%, DeepSeek-R1 58%, ASCO Assistant 67% (all P<.01); no hallucinated answers observed.
evidence.quote: Most errors were due to incorrect guideline selection or misinterpretation; no hallucinated answers were observed.

evidence.title: KT-LLM: an evidence-grounded and sequence text framework for auditable kidney transplant modeling
evidence.outcome: Evidence attribution and predictive calibration versus baselines when outputs are grounded in retrieved authoritative sources
evidence.effect: KT-LLM, with retrieval-augmented grounding in Banff, OPTN and SRTR documents, outperformed strong baselines in evidence attribution and predictive calibration; no numbers reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: On de-identified OPTN and UNOS cohorts, KT-LLM outperformed strong baselines in evidence attribution and predictive calibration.

evidence.title: A context-augmented large language model for accurate precision oncology medicine recommendations
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of biomarker-driven treatment recommendations, RAG-LLM using MOAlmanac versus LLM-only
evidence.effect: RAG-LLM reached up to 95% accuracy on synthetic queries and 93% on real-world oncologist queries; it was benchmarked against an LLM-only approach, but no LLM-only figures are given in the text.
evidence.quote: Our RAG-LLM achieved up to 95% accuracy on synthetic queries and 93% on real-world queries collected from practicing oncologists.

evidence.title: Reference Accuracy in Large Language Model Chatbots: A Metric for Inherent Misinformation?
evidence.venue: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
evidence.outcome: Reference accuracy with versus without web search retrieval

evidence.title: GastroTCM: a large language model assistant for gastroenterology in traditional Chinese medicine
evidence.outcome: Unsupported or hallucinated statements with RAG grounding, per TCM gastroenterologist review

evidence.quote: With guideline prompts, ChatGPT 4o's comprehensive answer rate increased to 93.33% (28/30), while DeepSeek's rate rose to 90.00% (27/30).

evidence.title: Superhuman performance on urology board questions using an explainable language model enhanced with European Association of Urology guidelines
evidence.venue: ESMO real world data and digital oncology
evidence.outcome: Rate of correct answers on urology board questions, RAG with EAU guidelines vs zero-shot GPT
evidence.effect: UroBot-4o (retrieval-augmented with 2023 EAU guidelines) averaged 88.4% correct vs 77.6% for zero-shot GPT-4o, a 10.8% gain; urologists averaged 68.7% per the literature.
evidence.quote: UroBot-4o achieved the highest RoCA, with an average of 88.4%, outperforming GPT-4o (77.6%) by 10.8%.

evidence.title: Deep research capabilities in GPT-5 thinking and Gemini 2.5 Pro improve citation integrity and concordance with American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons anterior cruciate ligament and rotator cuff guidelines
evidence.venue: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA
evidence.outcome: Citation integrity with versus without live web search/Deep Research grounding
evidence.effect: GPT-5 Thinking improved from 96.8% (231/239) to 100% (176/176); Gemini 2.5 Pro improved from 64.6% (173/268) to 98.6% (274/278) with Deep Research.
evidence.quote: Built-in LWS functions are particularly helpful in ensuring citation reliability.

evidence.title: Development and Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Radiology Guidelines

evidence.effect: Both RAG systems significantly outperformed standalone LLM; enhanced RAG factual accuracy 0.89 vs 0.68, completeness 4.20 vs 3.05, usefulness 3.99 vs 3.09 (5-point Likert).
evidence.quote: Both RAG systems significantly outperformed the standalone LLM in all metrics, with the enhanced model achieving the highest scores: Factual accuracy (0.89 vs. 0.68), completeness (4.20 vs. 3.05 on a 5-point Likert scale), and usefulness (3.99 vs. 3.09 on a 5-point Likert scale).

evidence.title: An LLM-Powered Clinical Calculator Chatbot Backed by Verifiable Clinical Calculators and their Metadata

evidence.quote: It eliminates calculation errors when prompted with complete sentences (0% vs. 16.8%) and greatly reduces them when prompted with medical shorthand (2.4% vs. 18%).

evidence.title: Improving electronic health record processing of large language models via retrieval-augmented generation: A case study on dietary supplements
evidence.venue: AMIA ... Annual Symposium proceedings. AMIA Symposium
evidence.outcome: LLM dietary supplement information extraction performance with versus without retrieval-augmented generation
evidence.effect: RAG enhanced LLM extraction of dietary supplement information from EHR text. Task-aligned retrieval outperformed reliance on model size or specialization. No numeric results reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: We demonstrate that retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) enhances LLMs for dietary supplement (DS) information extraction.

evidence.title: Performance of Enhanced Large Language Models on Prosthodontic Multiple-Choice Questions
evidence.outcome: Accuracy on prosthodontic MCQs with vs without retrieval-augmented enhancement (RAG, ICL, majority voting)
evidence.effect: Enhanced models significantly more accurate on Chinese MCQs (P < .001); higher but non-significant accuracy on English MCQs (P = .145). Knowledge errors fell significantly in Chinese (P < .008), not English (P = .604).
evidence.quote: Enhanced versions of both DeepSeek-R1 and OpenAI o1 achieved significant accuracy improvement compared with their base versions in Chinese-language multiple-choice questions (C-MCQs) (P < .001).

evidence.title: Evaluation of Large Language Models as Emergency Department Revisit Predictors

evidence.outcome: Effect of retrieval augmentation with 10 similar cases on LLM direct prediction F1

evidence.quote: The most significant gains were observed in GPT-4o (from F1=0.3403 to 0.3867) and Claude 3.7 (standard), with the latter achieving the highest overall F1 score of 0.4160 (95% CI [0.4024, 0.4294]) among direct prediction methods.

evidence.title: From Scores to Steps: Diagnosing and Improving LLM Performance in Evidence-Based Medical Calculations

evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLMs with and without retrieval-augmented generation plus code execution pipeline (MedRaC)

evidence.quote: Without any fine-tuning, MedRaC improves the accuracy of different LLMs from 16.35% up to 53.19%.

evidence.title: Cardiology knowledge assessment of retrieval-augmented open versus proprietary large language models

evidence.effect: All 14 models improved after RAG; open-weight Mistral Large 2 reached 78.0% (95% CI 73.9-81.5), comparable to GPT 4o. RAG was particularly beneficial for smaller models.
evidence.quote: After RAG, all models improved, and open-weight models like Mistral Large 2 (78.0%, 95% CI: 73.9-81.5) performed comparably to proprietary alternatives like GPT 4o.

evidence.title: Performance of latest AI models, RAG, and MCP on lung cancer-related questions
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM answers to lung cancer guideline questions with vs without RAG or MCP
evidence.effect: Baseline accuracy 36-50% (o3 50%, GPT 48%, Gemini 48%, Grok 44%, Qwen 40%, Claude 36%); RAG or MCP significantly improved accuracy over baseline LLMs.
evidence.quote: However, implementing RAG (LLM-RAG) or MCP (LLM-MCP) significantly improved accuracy, with statistical differences observed between baseline LLMs and their RAG- or MCP-enhanced counterparts.

evidence.title: Automated Prediction of Radiological Protocols Using Retrieval Augmented Generation

evidence.quote: Paired bootstrap analyses revealed that RAG improved macro F1 at two of three sites (Arizona:: Δ =0.0306, p=0.0074; Florida: Δ =0.0245, p=0.0217) while maintaining equivalent weighted F1.

evidence.title: Concordance of ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and OpenEvidence with the 2024 AAOS guidelines on acute isolated meniscal pathology

evidence.effect: OpenEvidence 9/9 (100%) vs ChatGPT 8/9 (89%), Gemini and Claude 7/9 (78%); Cochran's Q = 3.00, p = 0.392, so no significant difference.

evidence.quote: The system achieved 99.0% accuracy (198/200), with perfect precision and 0.99 recall.

evidence.title: FedKGC: Federated Knowledge-Grounded Calibration Framework for Hallucination Mitigation in Medical LLMs
evidence.venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

evidence.title: Precision Grounding: augmenting large language models with evidence-based databases for trustworthy genetic variant summarization

evidence.effect: Precision Grounding outperformed web-search grounding, with significantly higher accuracy (4.76, +0.74) and completeness (4.94, +0.84) on 5-point Likert scale; fewer clinically significant hallucinations.

evidence.title: An automatic consult reply system for therapeutic plasma exchange using retrieval-augmented generation

evidence.effect: RAG configurations consistently outperformed non-RAG baselines across items, with largest gains in plasma-volume calculation and ASFA classification.

commentary.bottom_line: Most comparative tests, largely small and offline, suggest that grounding outputs in curated sources lowers hallucination and raises rated accuracy, and one real deployment reported hallucinations in 10% of grounded versus 38% of ungrounded answers. Two tests found that grounding degraded outputs or failed to prevent errors, and grounded systems still produced errors, so certainty is low.

perspectives.view: One real-deployment quasi-experiment found hallucinations in 5/52 (10%) of RAG answers versus 15/39 (38%) native answers (P=.002). Most other tests are offline, small, or confounded by model changes. One study with 80,502 expert annotations found that standard RAG lowered factuality by up to 6%. Inconsistency, indirectness, and risk of bias suggest low certainty.

Grounding appears to lower hallucination frequency without removing it. The grounded arm still hallucinated in 10% of answers in one deployment, and a model given source passages hallucinated in 19.7% of answers. A RAG chatbot produced unverified contact details in 4/20 distress probes. A RAG mental health classifier raised more false alarms. Grounded output may still need review.

Retrieval quality appears to determine whether grounding helps. In one evaluation only 22% of the top-16 retrieved passages were relevant. A guideline RAG produced zero verifiable citations, while a knowledge-graph design reached 100%. In one deployment, accuracy rose from 67% to 82% as knowledge hit rates rose from 86% to 100% across tuning rounds, which suggests curation requires sustained work.

Tests ran in Germany, Slovenia, China, Bangladesh, and India, and three were tagged as including non-English-speaking patients. One Caribbean tool cited verified local facilities in 28/28 queries versus 10/28 for ChatGPT. No test enrolled Medicaid, safety-net, or low-literacy patients in the United States. A descriptive RAG chatbot study with Medicaid caregivers reported 99% intent accuracy without an ungrounded comparator.

NIST AI 600-1 lists grounding and retrieval-augmented generation as one control among several that organizations may apply. The CHAI guide treats knowledge-base integration as a requirement for treatment-selection use cases. The endorsing sources are frameworks and commentaries, and none of the supplied tests addresses regulatory compliance or liability.

Cost and speed data are sparse. One oncology study found that a fixed high-end model cost more and received lower expert ratings than automatic model selection with context. One graph-grounded design reported lower latency than text-only RAG but gave no numbers. Repeated tuning rounds in one deployment suggest that knowledge-base upkeep requires ongoing staff time.

Three reported cases describe patients and families misled by false LLM information. Grounding in verified directories may help patients reach real services, since one Caribbean tool cited verified facilities in 28/28 queries. A RAG chatbot still invented contact details in 4/20 distress scenarios, which suggests that patients in crisis may need a direct route to a human.

commentary.research_gap: No randomized or controlled deployment study measures patient harm, clinician error correction, or downstream care outcomes for grounded versus ungrounded outputs. Few studies report retrieval precision alongside output quality, and few separate the effect of grounding from concurrent changes to the model or prompt. Head-to-head comparisons of retrieval designs, such as text RAG versus knowledge graphs, are rare, and no tests have been run in safety-net settings in the United States.
commentary.underserved_note: Several tests of the practice ran in Germany, Slovenia, China, Bangladesh, India, and the Caribbean, and three were tagged as including non-English-speaking patients. No test of the practice included Medicaid, safety-net, low-literacy, or limited English proficiency patients within health systems in the United States. The only study involving Medicaid caregivers was descriptive and lacked an ungrounded comparator, so it remains untested whether curated sources cover the services and languages these patients use.
